# Check out the latest Pod with the hosts of the Long Play Series.
---
| |
Jen Palmieri and Erinn Haines, hosts of the Long Play Series, joined us to look at rising voter participation, changing political coalitions, new candidates, and the organizing infrastructure taking shape across South Carolina and other Southern states. We examine why the South is far less politically settled than national coverage often suggests, how voting rights and gerrymandering are changing the stakes, and why Democrats may have more opportunities in the region than conventional wisdom allows. If you want to understand where American politics could be heading next, the South may be the place to look. [LISTEN UP! ](https://us.list-manage.com/p_mDcEgd5vv?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)

---
| |
Spartanburg County Council’s Public Safety Committee will host its second hearing on data centers on Wednesday, September 9, beginning at 5:30 PM in Council Chambers (366 N. Church Street). body:
Only three Senate races in the country are rated Toss-up by Inside Elections. Ours is one of them.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8864%2E582294%2EoygQPD)
Team,
**This week New Hampshire chose Chris Pappas to be our Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate.**
Thank you to everyone who knocked doors, made calls, and contributed what you could through emails like this one over the past year. **This happened because of you.**
We are officially in the general election, and we’re starting it in a position of strength.
_Now for the hard part._
Our opponent is John Sununu. He is a former U.S. Senator with the most recognizable last name in New Hampshire politics, and he will have every dollar national Republican groups can afford to send his way.
**Last week Inside Elections moved our race from Tilt Democratic to Toss-up.**
Here’s the current Senate map:
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260911_3.4AAfHk&refcode=em20260911-3&t=2&akid=8864%2E582294%2EoygQPD)
_Source: Inside Elections_
**There are only three Toss-up Senate races in the entire country, and New Hampshire is one of them.**
Here’s why that matters: Republicans currently hold 53 seats in the Senate. For Democrats to win the majority, we need to net four seats. Democrats already hold New Hampshire’s Senate seat, so this isn’t a pickup opportunity — it’s a must-hold. If we lose it, Democrats would need five pickups instead of four, and the path gets very narrow very quickly.
There is no Democratic Senate majority without a win in New Hampshire.
**The general election started on Wednesday.** We have 53 days to outwork and outcommunicate John Sununu, and the costs go up quickly from here: organizers in all ten counties of the state, TV and digital ads reserved before all the inventory evaporates, and the ability to answer every attack they lob at us.
That’s why we’re setting a critical goal: **raise $100,000 in the first 72 hours of the general election from emails like this one.**
**[Will you make your first general election contribution to Chris Pappas’s campaign today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260911_3.4AAfHk&refcode=em20260911-3&t=3&akid=8864%2E582294%2EoygQPD)**
**[Give now to keep NH blue »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260911_3.4AAfHk&refcode=em20260911-3&t=4&akid=8864%2E582294%2EoygQPD)**
Let’s go win.
Chris Pappas HQ
P.S. John Sununu’s campaign and the outside groups backing him aren’t waiting for the dust to settle. If you can please give before midnight tonight to help us reach our $100,000 fundraising goal and start the general election on the front foot: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_20260909_3?refcode=em20260909-3&personal;=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260911_3.4AAfHk&refcode=em20260911-3&t=5&akid=8864%2E582294%2EoygQPD)**
_If you’ve donated recently, by check, or using a different email address, thank you! Our records take time to update, but thank you for the support!_
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**

name: Carmela Conroy
subject: 25 years ago
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CONROY FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | | | | | |
Good afternoon,

September 11, 2001 was a sunny Tuesday morning in Washington, DC. That morning I went to the office early for a classified briefing, as I had just started a new assignment as a trade negotiator. When the briefing ended we exited the sound-proof room, we heard the fire alarms. As I headed down five flights of stairs to exit the Harry S Truman Building I could tell from the way people were moving: This. Was. Not. A. Drill.
We could see a pillar of smoke rising from the Pentagon. My friend Julie, a Foreign Service orientation classmate and coworker at Embassy Tokyo under Ambassador Tom Foley, joined me as we walked to Georgetown, across the Francis Scot Key Bridge, to her apartment in Arlington. It was hours before we could reach our families on the west coast to tell them we were okay.
A few hours later I took the eerily empty subway back to Foggy Bottom, retrieved my car, and drove by the Pentagon on my way home to Alexandria. Civilian and military law enforcement personnel and I made eye contact and nodded at each other as I passed, sad and sobered. If you’re old enough to remember this date 25 years ago, I’m sure you have your own memories of the day.
September 12, 2001 felt like a whole new world full of uncertainty—until I was recalled to “Ops,” the Secretary of State’s communications and briefing staff. My year-long assignment at the State Department’s Operations Center had ended September 7, and the senior watch officer needed me back. Secretary Colin Powell was taking back-to-back calls from foreign counterparts and Ops was hopping, connecting, documenting and transmitting to “need-to-know” offices across the federal government, what those foreign leaders had to say. I connected and listened and typed and transmitted over and over across three shifts that day.
From Russia to New Zealand, from Japan to South Africa, as if with one voice, they said:We are so sorry for your terrible loss.We are with you.We want to help.
And across the country, Americans flew the Stars and Stripes and we pulled together in mourning and resolve. One nation, indivisible. Today is a good day to connect with loved ones; mourn the dead; and fight like hell for the living.
9/11 shaped my view of the world, of our country, and it galvanized my commitment to democracy and national security. Reply to this email if you are moved to share your story of September 11.
In solidarity,Carmela

Peter,

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: An AI Insider Just Issued a Terrifying Warning
body:
Plus, New Ads, AI Politics & Remembering 9/11| New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/70yZIZN_JPg?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | An AI Insider Just Issued a Terrifying Warning!We use AI. You probably do too.
But when the people actually BUILDING this technology start publicly warning that they’re worried about where it’s headed, we think it’s worth paying attention.And one former Anthropic researcher just issued a warning that stopped us in our tracks.
🔥 THE PEOPLE BUILDING AI ARE SOUNDING THE ALARMJacob Coxon, who worked on AI research at Anthropic and previously at OpenAI, publicly quit and warned about the race toward increasingly powerful artificial intelligence. His concern? The companies developing this technology are racing toward super-intelligence without knowing for certain that humans will remain in control.
And he isn't alone.
Another Anthropic researcher publicly backed Coxon's concerns and said he believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI could cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade. We break down what they're saying — and why this conversation suddenly feels a lot less like science fiction.
Spoiler alert: Remember when The Terminator seemed completely ridiculous? It hits a little differently now.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/vwe8lMLGMjc?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |

🚨 AI IS ALREADY CHANGING OUR ELECTIONS
We don't even have to wait for super-intelligence to see a problem. The Paxton campaign in Texas has released an ad featuring an AI-generated James Talarico. The statements in the ad are based on positions and comments attributed to Talarico — but that's not actually Talarico standing there delivering those lines.
That's where we have a problem.
If campaigns normalize realistic AI versions of candidates, how long before voters can't tell what's real? And once voters stop believing their own eyes and ears, that's a much bigger problem than one political ad.
🌶️ TRUMP WANTS TO RENAME NEW MEXICO?!
Yes, this happened. President Trump floated the idea of changing New Mexico to “New America,” and New Mexico's political leaders quickly responded.
We have a slightly different reaction: Guys. He's trolling you.
Nobody is actually renaming New Mexico. Meanwhile, our state has plenty of REAL problems that deserve the attention of our elected officials.We break down the reaction — and why politicians continue taking the bait.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/LfB4QQnn8pd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

📺 HAALAND AND HULL HAVE NEW ADS
We finally have new campaign ads from both Deb Haaland and Gregg Hull in the New Mexico governor's race. And we're critiquing both of them.Haaland's ad surprised us with an incredibly dark portrayal of life in New Mexico: stretching meals, battling for homes and struggling to get by.
Gregg Hull takes a much more optimistic approach — but his ad is only 15 seconds long. Our take? He has a compelling story. Give voters enough time to hear it.
And yes, we're conservatives. But we're not going to tell you a Republican ad is great when we don't think it is. That's not what this show is.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/ty3Wio0I5J2?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🇺🇸 WE WILL NEVER FORGET
Friday marks another anniversary of September 11, 2001.
Mark and Krysty share their memories of that morning — where they were, who they called and the moment they realized America was under attack. Mark also remembers something almost unimaginable today: flying home the NIGHT BEFORE 9/11 with the cockpit door open.
Then we share an incredible story from actor James Woods.A month before the attacks, Woods was on a flight when four men caught his attention. Their behavior concerned him enough that he alerted the flight crew and said he believed they might be preparing to hijack the plane. After September 11, he called the FBI. What happened next is remarkable.
For those of us who remember that day, we have a responsibility to make sure our children understand it too. We can remember the evil that occurred without living in fear — and remember something else that happened afterward:For a brief moment, America came together.
We'd love to see some of that again.

name: Deb HQ
subject: The August rundown for you
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=1&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
# **Sandoval County Parade & Fair**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=2&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb was grateful for the warm welcome at the Sandoval County Parade! It was a great day celebrating local traditions, catching up with neighbors, and hearing directly from families across the county about what matters most to them. And of course, enjoying great food and even better company.
---
|
---
# **National Night Out**
---
[ ](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=3&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Safe communities are built on trust, strong neighborhoods, and people looking out for one another. At National Night Out, Deb joined Albuquerque families, neighbors, and local law enforcement to strengthen the partnerships that keep our communities safe. As Governor, Deb will continue building these partnerships and making sure communities have the resources and support they need to keep New Mexico safe for every family.
---
|
---
# **Gallup Inter-Tribal Indian Ceremonial Parade**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=4&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
New Mexico’s Tribal communities are an invaluable part of our state’s heritage, culture, and traditions. Deb was so happy to be back in Northwestern New Mexico to celebrate with the community at the 104th Inter-Tribal Indian Ceremonial Parade in Gallup. As a proud Pueblo woman, Deb understands the importance of listening to and working alongside Tribal communities. As Governor, she’ll make sure Tribal nations have a seat at the table and continue building strong, respectful relationships that honor their sovereignty, culture, and traditions.
---
|
---
# **Chama Days Parade**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=5&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb had a great time at the Chama Days Parade! Chama Days is a wonderful opportunity for families and neighbors to come together, enjoy the festivities, and celebrate the traditions that make Chama so special. Deb was grateful for the warm welcome and happy to celebrate with the community. Happy Chama Days!
---
|
---
# **Chaco Canyon**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=6&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb was grateful to spend time at Chaco Canyon, a place that carries generations of history, culture, and meaning for New Mexico’s Tribal communities. Standing among the ancient sites, Deb reflected on the generations who have cared for and fought to protect this sacred landscape. Chaco is more than a historic site. It is a living connection to the people and communities who have called this land home for generations.

That’s why Deb has always fought to protect Chaco. As Secretary of the Interior, she helped establish a 20-year withdrawal of federal lands within 10 miles of the park from new oil and gas leasing and mining claims. Now, those protections are under threat. The Trump administration is considering reversing them and reopening the Greater Chaco landscape to new mineral development. Deb knows what is at stake, and she’ll continue fighting to protect Chaco, honor Tribal sovereignty, and make sure this sacred landscape is here for generations to come.
---
|
---
# **NM School for the Blind Tour**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=7&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
In Alamogordo, Deb toured the New Mexico School for the Blind to learn more about how educators help visually impaired students build skills, confidence, and independence. From the classroom to independent living, students are gaining the tools they need to navigate life on their own terms. Deb will work to make sure every New Mexico student has the support and opportunities they need to learn, grow, and thrive.
---
|
---
# **First We Bombed NM Screening**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=8&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
New Mexico’s Downwinders have spent generations fighting for the recognition and justice they deserve. Deb was grateful to be in Alamogordo for a screening of First We Bombed New Mexico and to spend time with the families who have carried this fight forward for decades. Their stories are part of New Mexico’s story, and a reminder of the generations who have fought to make sure their communities are seen and heard. As Governor, Deb will make sure Downwinders and uranium workers can access the compensation they deserve and have support every step of the way.
---
|
---
# **Mescalero Public Safety Visit**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=9&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
In Mescalero, Deb saw the work underway to build a new facility that will provide essential supplies, shelter, and support when disaster strikes. Having a place where families can turn during an emergency is critical to helping communities prepare and recover. As Governor, Deb will work to ensure communities across New Mexico have the resources and infrastructure they need to prepare for, respond to, and recover from natural disasters.
---
|
---
# **Ruidoso Burn Scar**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=10&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb joined Congresswoman Melanie Stansbury in Ruidoso to see the burn scars firsthand and hear from families still recovering from devastating floods and the fires that preceded them.

The road to recovery doesn’t end when the flames are out and the smoke has cleared. As Governor, Deb will work alongside communities like Ruidoso to rebuild, strengthen infrastructure, and ensure New Mexico is better prepared for the disasters ahead.
---
|
---
# **Indian Market**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=11&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb loved spending Indian Market weekend in Santa Fe surrounded by so much talent, tradition, and creativity. She was proud to celebrate the Native artists who bring their stories, cultures, and traditions to life through their work. Indian Market is a special part of New Mexico, and Deb is always grateful for the opportunity to celebrate the artists and communities who make it so meaningful.
---
|
---
# **Los Lunas Blvd**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=12&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb spent time in Los Lunas with Mayor Charles Griego learning about the work underway to support this growing community. She visited the Los Lunas Boulevard construction site, where the project will improve traffic flow, public safety, emergency response, and connectivity while creating new opportunities for the community.
---
|
---
# **Juniper Sol Community Solar Garden**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=13&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Juniper Sol Community Solar Garden is making the cost-saving benefits of renewable energy accessible to all, including renters and those who can’t afford the upfront installation of solar.
Here in New Mexico, we are blessed with vast renewable energy sources, including over 300 days of sun. By leaning into our resources, we can bring down utility costs for New Mexicans.
Deb was happy to be at Juniper Sol’s ribbon-cutting ceremony. As Governor, she’ll continue to work with and support energy initiatives like these that lower costs and improve life for New Mexicans across the state.
---
|
---
# **NM Innovation Hub**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=14&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
At the New Mexico Innovation Hub, Deb saw the work being done to grow New Mexico’s startup ecosystem, bring new technologies to market, and create opportunities right here at home.
New Mexico has the talent and resources to compete with anyone. As Governor, Deb will make sure the jobs and opportunities created benefit New Mexicans.
---
|
---
# **Grants Community Garden**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=15&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
New Mexicans know how to show up for each other. Deb enjoyed seeing the work the Grants Community Pantry is doing to make sure their neighbors have food on the table and the support they need.
---
|
---
# **Deming Duck Races Parade**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=16&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
New Mexico has one-of-a-kind traditions! Deb never misses an opportunity to celebrate with families right in their own communities. Thank you for the warm welcome at the Deming Duck Races Parade!🐥💛
---
|
---
# **Geothermal Tour**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=17&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
New Mexico has the resources we need to power our own future.
Deb toured the Lightning Dock geothermal plant to see firsthand how we can harness the energy beneath our feet to create good-paying jobs, strengthen our energy independence, and lower utility costs for families.
As Governor, Deb will go all in on New Mexico-made energy, from our 300 days of sunshine and incredible wind to our untapped geothermal potential. Together, we can build an energy economy that lowers costs for New Mexicans and keeps our state leading the way.
---
|
---
# **NMSU Women’s Soccer Game**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=18&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb spent an afternoon soaking up some sun and soccer with the NMSU Women’s Soccer team! Go Aggies!
---
|
---
# **NM Tech Tour**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=19&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb had a great visit to NM Tech, where she learned more about their work in water mapping and cleaning up water pollution in our state. Deb is committed to building a healthy New Mexico, starting with clean water and removing legacy pollution.
---
|
---
# **Seco Spice**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=20&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb visited Seco Spice to see how New Mexico chile is processed and prepared, then spent time at a local farm learning from the people who keep our agricultural communities strong. She’s grateful to the farmers, workers, and families who keep these traditions alive generation after generation. There’s nothing quite like chile season! 🌶️
---
|
---
# **Pacific Fusion Groundbreaking**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=21&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
Deb broke ground at Pacific Fusion’s new research and manufacturing campus right here in Albuquerque. New Mexico has the talent, labs, and ingenuity to lead the next generation of clean energy innovation. Investments like this mean good-paying jobs, a stronger economy, and new opportunities for New Mexicans. As Governor, Deb will work to make sure the technologies of the future are built and supported right here in New Mexico.
---
|
---
# **CREDA**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=22&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
At the CREDA gubernatorial forum, Deb shared her plan to build more housing across New Mexico by cutting unnecessary red tape, speeding up permitting, lowering construction costs, and helping more first-time homebuyers afford a home.
New Mexicans deserve a safe, affordable place to call home — without having to choose between paying the rent and putting food on the table.
We know the problem. Now it’s time to get to work and get homes built for New Mexicans.
---
|
---
# **Roadrunnin’ Tour**
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=23&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
In August, Deb kicked off her Roadrunnin’ Tour, her third statewide tour to visit all 33 counties across New Mexico. She met with voters in 14 communities, hearing directly from New Mexicans about what matters most to their families and communities. Everywhere she goes, Deb hears the same priorities: better education, reliable healthcare, clean water, and safer communities. Deb is excited to keep hitting the road, listening to New Mexicans, and bringing their voices with her every step of the way.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16523?refcode=jtk1368-ot-nd&t=24&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)
---
# **[**Outside: Op-Ed: The Places that Shape Us Cannot Be Recreated After Trump Opens Them Up**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16760?t=25&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)**
---
|
---
# **[High Country News: Deb Haaland’s vision for New Mexico comes from tradition](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16761?t=26&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)**
---
|
---
# **[Native News Online: New Mexico Dem governor nominee Haaland touts permitting ‘shot clock’ in visit to housing project](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16762?t=27&akid=12420%2E400544%2E_wxTV3)**
---
|
---

subject: It’s simple.
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Over the next few weeks, Greg Abbott is going to start spending _millions_ from his massive war chest to buy a fourth term in our tied race for Texas Governor.
We want to make one thing clear — our job isn't to match Greg Abbott dollar for dollar. We don't have corporate megadonors writing blank checks, and we don't need them.
**Our job is simply to raise enough money to reach voters and share our vision for Texas.**
If we have the resources to tell our story, we win this thing. It’s that simple.
In a grassroots-powered campaign like ours, every single dollar goes directly toward reaching voters across Texas.
**[Will you chip in $5 right now to help us share our message and win this race?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260911_4_money.ak9oqY&refcode=em20260911-2095&amount=5&t=1&akid=2095%2E299639%2EOmCrZk)**

Thank you,

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Education Department Watchdog: School Insiders Have Stolen Nearly $71 Million in Fraud Schemes
body:
Navy Wastes $3.4 Billion on Inoperable Submarines

[INSIDE JW]

EDUCATION DEPARTMENT WATCHDOG: SCHOOL INSIDERS HAVE STOLEN NEARLY $71
MILLION IN FRAUD SCHEMES

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38622&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1UZlNLNmFtbThmYyZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=5e9dc80e9212b82f58c52a3c0299dcf58b0a64ad2b926008b051927cb9e51bb1]

Fraud is costing America’s schools millions of dollars, and many of
the perpetrators are not outsiders—they are the officials and
employees entrusted with running the nation’s public education
system. Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog has some shocking details
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38623&F=T&&hash=89b1203ba50e6a65c30eb46354f362ce63ee2981eb489a8625359c6356ea27ed

> As the state of public education in the U.S. sinks to a historic low
> with consistent declines in math and reading scores, those hired by
> local governments to run the nation’s failing elementary, middle
> and high school campuses commit tens of millions of dollars in
> fraud. They include state and district superintendents, high-ranking
> school officials and lower level staff as well as charter school
> administrators. In the last five years alone, the public servants
> charged with educating children have operated at least 130
> fraudulent schemes that have robbed schools of nearly $71 million. A
> new audit
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38624&F=T&&hash=41009d86eb016ac9c8e279330a9b7d497a5d4d327db107778f60024ea9b8ecf2]
> released by the Department of Education Inspector General (IG) calls
> them “bad actors” who were mostly exposed via a hotline portal
> operated by the watchdog. The probe resulted in 98 criminal and
> civil cases, 74 suspensions and 13 administrative actions.
> “Individuals who commit K–12 fraud frequently operate within the
> school system itself,” according to the Education watchdog.
> “These perpetrators have included State Superintendents of
> Education, charter school leaders, district superintendents and
> other high-ranking school officials, and school employees at all
> levels, as well as school vendors.”
>
> Created by Jimmy Carter in 1979, the Department of Education (ED) is
> legally responsible for administering more than 100 programs and
> distributing billions of dollars annually to state and local
> education agencies, schools, organizations, and other entities that
> support students nationwide. However, the report says criminals
> target these programs each year, including special education,
> vocational rehabilitation, and Title I funds for school districts
> serving low-income families. Investigators found that these “bad
> actors”—insiders at taxpayer-funded schools across the
> country—abuse ED programs and intentionally misuse or embezzle
> funds meant to help students, schools, and teachers. Detecting the
> fraud is especially difficult because K–12 funding is
> decentralized across thousands of independent school districts
> around the country. Most federal education funds flow to state
> education entities, which then distribute money to local agencies,
> school districts, and individual schools. “Federal dollars are
> often blended with State and local funds and tracked through
> localized bookkeeping practices—which makes oversight more
> complex,” the new report reveals.
>
> Evidently, this is why the ED watchdog relies heavily on complaints
> from individuals within school systems. That means the problem is
> surely much worse than the cases documented in the recently
> published report, which covers fiscal years 2020 through 2025.
> Investigations fell primarily within five categories: charter school
> fraud, public corruption, illicit schemes involving programs
> authorized under a decades-old law (Elementary and Secondary
> Education Act—ESEA) to provide disadvantaged students with a
> quality education, tutoring and academic support program fraud as
> well as scams involving emergency relief programs. The cases
> involving charter schools, which are publicly funded with no
> oversight, include embezzlement, inflated student enrollment
> numbers, ghost students or staff and fake invoicing schemes. Public
> corruption cases, which include abuse of position by school
> officials or employees for personal gain, uncovered bribery and
> kickback schemes, irregularities in contract awards and criminal
> conflicts of interest.
>
> Embezzlement, misuse of funds and false representation were the key
> offenses committed by public officials running school programs
> funded under ESEA, which delivers financial assistance to districts
> and campuses that serve children from low-income families. Only six
> percent of the stolen money has been recovered, however.
> Taxpayer-funded tutoring and academic support programs for primarily
> students in high-poverty, low-performing schools were also raided by
> crooked education officials who embezzled funds, filed false
> invoices and reported ghost students to collect more money. As for
> emergency relief, Congress provided billions of dollars in funding
> to help K-12 schools and districts nationwide meet the educational
> needs of students affected by hurricanes and wildfires and billions
> more during the coronavirus pandemic, making the broad cash giveaway
> an easy target for corrupt educators. The audit found that those
> crimes “predominately involved false claims, mismanagement, or
> misuse of funds.”

ICE ARRESTS 1,328 CRIMINAL ALIENS IN WASHINGTON SUBURBS IN TWO-WEEK
SWEEP

More than 1,300 illegal immigrants with criminal records—including
murderers, rapists, kidnappers, arsonists, drug traffickers and
members of violent transnational gangs—were arrested in a two-week
federal crackdown across the Washington, D.C., suburbs of Virginia and
Maryland. Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog has the details
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38625&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvb3Zlci0xMzAwLWNyaW1pbmFsLWFsaWVucy1hcnJlc3RlZC9dOj91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=a5c2e2b46311f802d33e726b739d3730714909ce36da02adbb71361994537044

> Illustrating once again how sanctuary policies endanger American
> communities by harboring criminal aliens, more than 1,300 illegal
> immigrants with serious criminal records have lived freely for an
> unknown period in two suburbs surrounding the nation’s capital.
> Even after getting arrested by local police, convicted or serving
> time for violent felonies, the foreign perpetrators were released by
> open border officials rather than turned over to federal authorities
> for removal. The offenders include murderers, rapists, kidnappers,
> arsonists, drug traffickers, and members of transnational criminal
> street gangs such as the famously violent Tren de Aragua, Mara
> Salvatrucha (MS-13) and 18th Street.
>
> In a significant development unlikely to receive mainstream media
> coverage, a federal crackdown recently arrested the
> offenders—1,328 in all—in the Washington, D.C. suburbs of
> Virginia and Maryland. Conducted by Immigration and Customs
> Enforcement (ICE), the two-week sweep, coined Operation Safe
> Community
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38626&F=T&&hash=35fa957a6870f6175fe6f66c49ee44e9db83bb82803985b3795b4c652659015a],
> comes on the heels of a similar roundup in Georgia that took more
> than 1,200 alien criminals off the streets. “When sanctuary
> politicians refuse to work with ICE, they force our officers to make
> these arrests at large in the communities–creating a more
> dangerous environment for our officers, the aliens we are arresting,
> and the general public,” said ICE Enforcement and Removal
> Operations (ERO) Acting Assistant Director Patricia Hyde. “We
> could be using one or two officers to make a custodial arrest in the
> security of a jail cell; however, because sanctuary politicians
> refuse to cooperate, we have to expend time, manpower, and resources
> to arrest these aliens on the streets.”
>
> This has long been a nationwide problem as local governments across
> the U.S. shield illegal immigrants—even those convicted of violent
> crimes—by refusing to participate in 287(g)
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=15114&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaWNlLmdvdi8yODdnP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=7a48c681badb81fd99f2f96b86a9ff8e3a39bd149c276f74efe28f90e4ceb744], a federal-local partnership that
> notifies ICE when inmates are in the country illegally so they can
> be deported rather than released into American communities. Less
> than a year ago, Judicial Watch reported
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85369&L=38627&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvc3RhdGVzLXJlbGVhc2UtOTAwMC1jcmltaW5hbC1hbGllbnMvXXRoYXQ/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=b150cef90d44677d46e10187dd0e9cf4f5d2db6670d94435bc4457145e948195
> two sanctuary states alone, New York and Illinois, released nearly
> 9,000 criminal aliens from jails and prisons during a 10-month
> period, defying ICE detainers to remove them. Among the offenders
> protected by the sanctuary policies in the two states were
> murderers, terrorists, sexual predators, kidnappers, and serious
> drug offenders. A Turkish Known or Suspected Terrorist (KST) named
> Selman Cevik jailed for first degree menacing and harassment as well
> a rapist and two known gang members were let go by New York
> officials. Illinois released a Mexican man convicted of three counts
> of aggravated kidnapping/ransom and another convicted for predatory
> criminal sex assault of a child. It is not clear if any of the New
> York or Illinois criminal aliens have been apprehended by ICE since
> local officials released them.
>
> In the recent Operation Safe Community hundreds of the criminal
> aliens roaming the capital area had convictions for major crimes in
> the U.S. and clearly benefitted from the protection of sanctuary
> policies in counties throughout Virginia and Maryland. Others had
> serious felony charges or were known members of violent street
> gangs. Without cooperation from local authorities, tracking them
> down required more federal resources as well as time. “Our
> officers are the best in the world at finding people who do not want
> to be located,” said Hyde, the ICE ERO assistant director.
> “That’s exactly what we did throughout the course of this
> operation. Removing these criminal alien offenders from Virginia and
> Maryland neighborhoods makes for much safer communities, and that is
> exactly what the men and women of ICE work to accomplish every day
> across our great nation.”
>
> ICE, which is part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS),
> includes mug shots and a detailed criminal history of those
> apprehended in the recent operation surrounding the nation’s
> capital. Among them is German Mejia-Baires, a previously deported
> MS-13 gang member from El Salvador arrested for felony malicious
> wounding, driving while intoxicated and shoplifting. Haitian
> national Actionel Pierre, was free despite being wanted for
> attempted murder, two counts of assault, possession of a dangerous
> weapon with intent to injure, and reckless endangerment. Guatemalan
> Angel Gabriel Ortiz-Hernandez has a criminal history that includes
> rape of a mentally incapacitated victim and two counts of aggravated
> sexual battery of an incapacitated victim. Previously deported
> Jamaican Rowan Andrew Brown’s criminal history includes
> kidnapping, two counts of identity theft and fraud. Mexican Julio
> Hector Carranza-Rojano has charges for felony aggravated sexual
> battery, driving while intoxicated and leaving the scene of an
> accident.

Until next week,

clean_body: Navy Wastes $3.4 Billion on Inoperable Submarines [INSIDE JW] EDUCATION DEPARTMENT WATCHDOG: SCHOOL INSIDERS HAVE STOLEN NEARLY $71 MILLION IN FRAUD SCHEMES [] Fraud is costing America’s schools millions of dollars, and many of the perpetrators are not outsiders—they are the officials and employees entrusted with running the nation’s public education system. Our Corruption Chronicles blog has some shocking details [ As the state of public education in the U.S. sinks to a historic low with consistent declines in math and reading scores, those hired by local governments to run the nation’s failing elementary, middle and high school campuses commit tens of millions of dollars in fraud. They include state and district superintendents, high-ranking school officials and lower level staff as well as charter school administrators. In the last five years alone, the public servants charged with educating children have operated at least 130 fraudulent schemes that have robbed schools of nearly $71 million. A new audit [] released by the Department of Education Inspector General (IG) calls them “bad actors” who were mostly exposed via a hotline portal operated by the watchdog. The probe resulted in 98 criminal and civil cases, 74 suspensions and 13 administrative actions. “Individuals who commit K–12 fraud frequently operate within the school system itself,” according to the Education watchdog. “These perpetrators have included State Superintendents of Education, charter school leaders, district superintendents and other high-ranking school officials, and school employees at all levels, as well as school vendors.” Created by Jimmy Carter in 1979, the Department of Education (ED) is legally responsible for administering more than 100 programs and distributing billions of dollars annually to state and local education agencies, schools, organizations, and other entities that support students nationwide. However, the report says criminals target these programs each year, including special education, vocational rehabilitation, and Title I funds for school districts serving low-income families. Investigators found that these “bad actors”—insiders at taxpayer-funded schools across the country—abuse ED programs and intentionally misuse or embezzle funds meant to help students, schools, and teachers. Detecting the fraud is especially difficult because K–12 funding is decentralized across thousands of independent school districts around the country. Most federal education funds flow to state education entities, which then distribute money to local agencies, school districts, and individual schools. “Federal dollars are often blended with State and local funds and tracked through localized bookkeeping practices—which makes oversight more complex,” the new report reveals. Evidently, this is why the ED watchdog relies heavily on complaints from individuals within school systems. That means the problem is surely much worse than the cases documented in the recently published report, which covers fiscal years 2020 through 2025. Investigations fell primarily within five categories: charter school fraud, public corruption, illicit schemes involving programs authorized under a decades-old law (Elementary and Secondary Education Act—ESEA) to provide disadvantaged students with a quality education, tutoring and academic support program fraud as well as scams involving emergency relief programs. The cases involving charter schools, which are publicly funded with no oversight, include embezzlement, inflated student enrollment numbers, ghost students or staff and fake invoicing schemes. Public corruption cases, which include abuse of position by school officials or employees for personal gain, uncovered bribery and kickback schemes, irregularities in contract awards and criminal conflicts of interest. Embezzlement, misuse of funds and false representation were the key offenses committed by public officials running school programs funded under ESEA, which delivers financial assistance to districts and campuses that serve children from low-income families. Only six percent of the stolen money has been recovered, however. Taxpayer-funded tutoring and academic support programs for primarily students in high-poverty, low-performing schools were also raided by crooked education officials who embezzled funds, filed false invoices and reported ghost students to collect more money. As for emergency relief, Congress provided billions of dollars in funding to help K-12 schools and districts nationwide meet the educational needs of students affected by hurricanes and wildfires and billions more during the coronavirus pandemic, making the broad cash giveaway an easy target for corrupt educators. The audit found that those crimes “predominately involved false claims, mismanagement, or misuse of funds.” ICE ARRESTS 1,328 CRIMINAL ALIENS IN WASHINGTON SUBURBS IN TWO-WEEK SWEEP More than 1,300 illegal immigrants with criminal records—including murderers, rapists, kidnappers, arsonists, drug traffickers and members of violent transnational gangs—were arrested in a two-week federal crackdown across the Washington, D.C., suburbs of Virginia and Maryland. Our Corruption Chronicles blog has the details [ Illustrating once again how sanctuary policies endanger American communities by harboring criminal aliens, more than 1,300 illegal immigrants with serious criminal records have lived freely for an unknown period in two suburbs surrounding the nation’s capital. Even after getting arrested by local police, convicted or serving time for violent felonies, the foreign perpetrators were released by open border officials rather than turned over to federal authorities for removal. The offenders include murderers, rapists, kidnappers, arsonists, drug traffickers, and members of transnational criminal street gangs such as the famously violent Tren de Aragua, Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) and 18th Street. In a significant development unlikely to receive mainstream media coverage, a federal crackdown recently arrested the offenders—1,328 in all—in the Washington, D.C. suburbs of Virginia and Maryland. Conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the two-week sweep, coined Operation Safe Community [], comes on the heels of a similar roundup in Georgia that took more than 1,200 alien criminals off the streets. “When sanctuary politicians refuse to work with ICE, they force our officers to make these arrests at large in the communities–creating a more dangerous environment for our officers, the aliens we are arresting, and the general public,” said ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Acting Assistant Director Patricia Hyde. “We could be using one or two officers to make a custodial arrest in the security of a jail cell; however, because sanctuary politicians refuse to cooperate, we have to expend time, manpower, and resources to arrest these aliens on the streets.” This has long been a nationwide problem as local governments across the U.S. shield illegal immigrants—even those convicted of violent crimes—by refusing to participate in 287(g) [], a federal-local partnership that notifies ICE when inmates are in the country illegally so they can be deported rather than released into American communities. Less than a year ago, Judicial Watch reported [ two sanctuary states alone, New York and Illinois, released nearly 9,000 criminal aliens from jails and prisons during a 10-month period, defying ICE detainers to remove them. Among the offenders protected by the sanctuary policies in the two states were murderers, terrorists, sexual predators, kidnappers, and serious drug offenders. A Turkish Known or Suspected Terrorist (KST) named Selman Cevik jailed for first degree menacing and harassment as well a rapist and two known gang members were let go by New York officials. Illinois released a Mexican man convicted of three counts of aggravated kidnapping/ransom and another convicted for predatory criminal sex assault of a child. It is not clear if any of the New York or Illinois criminal aliens have been apprehended by ICE since local officials released them. In the recent Operation Safe Community hundreds of the criminal aliens roaming the capital area had convictions for major crimes in the U.S. and clearly benefitted from the protection of sanctuary policies in counties throughout Virginia and Maryland. Others had serious felony charges or were known members of violent street gangs. Without cooperation from local authorities, tracking them down required more federal resources as well as time. “Our officers are the best in the world at finding people who do not want to be located,” said Hyde, the ICE ERO assistant director. “That’s exactly what we did throughout the course of this operation. Removing these criminal alien offenders from Virginia and Maryland neighborhoods makes for much safer communities, and that is exactly what the men and women of ICE work to accomplish every day across our great nation.” ICE, which is part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), includes mug shots and a detailed criminal history of those apprehended in the recent operation surrounding the nation’s capital. Let’s take back what belongs to us.
| Friend, this is Adam Schiff.

Investigators in my office uncovered the contracts behind the banners of Donald Trump's face now hanging on federal buildings across Washington — the largest of them eight stories tall at the Department of Health and Human Services, with "America First" printed beside it: [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/130121?t=6&akid=28733%2E878179%2EXnN3jJ) | [ DONATE TO FIGHT BACK » ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/130121?t=7&akid=28733%2E878179%2EXnN3jJ)
---
Here’s what we uncovered:

The American people paid for every inch of it, and we have the receipts. $114,000 from the FAA. $39,000 from Interior. A third check from the Labor Department.

The list goes on and on.

**Congress long ago outlawed spending taxpayer dollars on propaganda and self-aggrandizement, and an eight-story-high Donald Trump head certainly qualifies.**

Because I spent years as a federal prosecutor, and I know a pattern of intent when I see one. In every country where democracy gave way to one man, the faces went up on the government buildings first. Not as decoration, and not even as vanity — but to teach the people who paid for those buildings a simple lesson: _all of this belongs to him now._

And yet not one of those buildings belongs to Donald Trump. They belong to the American people, to the taxpayers who funded them. We were never asked, and we do not have to accept it.

There is one check on this president that he cannot fire and cannot intimidate: a Democratic Senate, with the gavels and subpoena power to hold him to account.

Peter,
Another federal agency has joined Trump's campaign to weaponize the federal government against the American people in the upcoming midterm elections -- alongside the FBI, DHS, ICE, USPS, DOJ, and the U.S. Census Bureau.
This time it's the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), and its weapon is blatant, unconstitutional censorship of a Democratic candidate on national television.
Last night, Jimmy Kimmel dropped a bombshell on his show: an interview with Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico had been blocked from airing by Trump's FCC.

body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260912-61808&t=1001&akid=61808%2E1407376%2ESd22kZ ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260912-61808&t=1002&akid=61808%2E1407376%2ESd22kZ ]Demand Justice PAC

The Supreme
Court is handing over our elections to the highest bidder.

In their latest move, the Court cleared the way for wealthy party
committees to flood the airwaves with discounted political ads.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260912.I3JJtp&refcode=em20260912-61808&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61808%2E1407376%2ESd22kZ ]Headline from NBC News: 'Supreme Court backs Republicans in election ad
rate dispute: Republicans asked the court to allow party committees to
receive the same ad discounts that candidates themselves benefit from.'

This is not a Court working to strengthen our democracy. It’s a Court
hell-bent on destroying it.

Here’s what happened:

* The Court allowed a discounted rate for party ads, ensuring committees
get the same reduced pricing that individual candidates already do.
* They did this at the GOP’s and Trump’s request to block an appeals
court order that had stopped these discounts.
* They rigged the playing field, allowing Republican committees to pour
even more money into the airwaves for less — burying grassroots
campaigns that don’t have cash-flush committees bankrolling them.

This is a deliberate effort to tilt the scales of power toward the GOP,
corporate interests, and billionaire donors. By enabling wealthy
committees to saturate the airwaves, this ruling threatens to silence
voters and overwhelm local campaign messaging.

We refuse to let a Court that's supposed to be neutral hand Republicans a
financial advantage in our elections. Demand Justice PAC is organizing on
the front lines to push back against this abuse of power and fight for
real Court reform — because the outcome should be decided by voters, not
justices picking winners.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260912.I3JJtp&refcode=em20260912-61808&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=61808%2E1407376%2ESd22kZ ]Fuel the fight: Chip in $5 today to Demand Justice PAC
as we work to hold the Court accountable and protect free and fair
elections.

## Gas, Diesel Costs Drive August Inflation
Consumer prices rose [3.4% in August](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAMhp8mbEFOQuAyZOjCdl07Ih9x7lLlCAo-UN--opX6At0sfZb9f__Hdbpiymm5v-OTPMcyLXRsmZipTvi6vzZOS8zIqSwnWXGlmicNupfgpNITzpx2mjpsgo9EmkxDXg0Xp2GwVjUPr5SJFKw1DlQEZaLtEa2DDtDo6OYm-fMeOKUVgO1cG4A67N1l6MN8M2RFBxQSl9p-lrTwg2L-KjvVdi7PJvsH87oJ8yb0KPR4HEc737Yz7cmFHs9R6PFXR85rkpXWUln-qclIQVZkOvea6sN6pJzT1g-ig_sTU_55xf9saPf6OwAA___efnyi) from a year earlier, matching July's pace but coming in slightly above economists' forecasts. The odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week rose to 90% after the report. On Friday, the Labor Department said gasoline prices accounted for more than one-third of the monthly increase in the CPI report. Gasoline is up 27.4% from a year ago, although it increased 3.9% in August from the prior month. Meanwhile, [diesel hit a record $6.06 a gallon](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-upCAUh58GOw0eEaSg2MZutt3SMHB0zgbBAI6Zt7_xFvcFbv0lvz_fv8fysBQobn_tjqauaYl4lYC1Yl7suZ2lUlyDrZTiTQ57YA4LcJAt120Pi3WV3rgI23izIgIODZpeTRq4Gse-eRmllBNSSLkK67RXOK2T8AjQTzD5gTdk7jyue-g5H4XuPEdhpZ6U9O454MgER0815e5_olhfuIZPemPuXNqbYF61HoUNfxjMDObrurr4dPfamzOYn2ehiKUwmDFi3j4MZk9YMLQZXcq-PTI5bGs-96P9-dtmF-2o5SSGJht_XBQCFamY4NtuKXy3119Kexv4CgAA__97_YNm) on Friday, up 63% from a year ago. Because diesel powers the trucks and trains that move goods across the country, the surge is expected to ripple through consumer prices for months. Core prices, which strip out food and energy, jumped [0.3% for the month](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9utTAMR58mbKDEhH9Dhm9hu9_aEZlgLm5DgsAX1LevaKW-QOdjHev83h7DAzlwfP7HlZzMaYh0HYFEaB_w9XwdwnEOKJziTTbcaA8DaKhz3eUGBvTCJw0Ws8nNREBlRs40bQe6qSqTLc7Xo7eVwcYiNVSaFnVbzYS-xHGEWmfsbp_uDBitK9sVkyaLddc29eTHkiplNU0saS_eE0dZaA6f6aS98GnNgltEtkOV_xT0CvrrugofR39DBf2tVtDrTkFvjILeb5z_NuXjTvgxpSvmP7X5fV8ssoZsd9N2cQh81I2y-rkih--P8sehTgdfAQAA__-F8nz4), also a bit higher than expected.
## Newspapers Hit by National Wave of Layoffs
One of America's largest newspaper chains cut more than [90 journalists](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7MYAwuKLahe9tuiebhcTIrYyN7kqf8_Yr8wtbn6uje--dr-0JOnO-_8aBFYtky_bREIlQ3fN6fTTjHhMIlX-TEk2rawIDTxuseNtyFX7RZ7MISiYCGjpZ-mj2YaRz77rG4KVg3Uw-Dc5bA23nGHicX4uBhHHzHy-UzvofemNH6WzBk0fl5cmH_HmhU1lBgKfX2t3CWB8X0Li-qt70cXVoeImdTwy8Fq4I1v8_S5EIK1kusYDVewdobBetBgVHBumPiWGpm1NeuWsrRdKCdDxQKmrOWB-nvVEpgaqJreeagS9QJ3yXGprHpj0vfGbM0vT9TatqaK9MEY1SwdnUJ5w-nxM1Nypr7gZw-peU_v34t8C8AAP__Uo2Uig) nationally across at least 13 papers Thursday, with some newsrooms losing up to 40% of their staff in McClatchy's most severe layoffs in years. _The Fresno Bee_ was left with roughly a dozen reporters to cover California's fifth-largest city. _The Miami Herald_ , which once employed 300 journalists, will now have [fewer than 50](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-OrCAYBfCnwU7DH8WhoLiN3dx2S4PwoewiGPhmjG-_cYt9ga1Pcn455-M5P02IIa3_zQ4afZ4TnDUCIpTZvNZXxZB8NBhyupPDHFDizCmXLVUt47OxGN4w96Zx2gNwEA1oNj4Up-MwsGbTQjoqBHMWpLBLzwRV6uFAqGWRfhHQBH33UcU4o3ToVeco9EaqxyidXQQMpKfgAubSfeaQcAMfr_yG0tm8N1FviEcl4h_hE-HTeZ7dka-EULpcVsKn5VVDglrbM5cvwqdbI3zarY0G7Xa1O7hg2t99tY3myt5XwqemaHecIcZQ5Uh6uu4mxB8X_3jXW_PvAAAA__-0hYGB). Papers in Idaho, Kansas City, Charlotte, and Kentucky were also hit. McClatchy, owned by hedge fund Chatham Asset Management since its 2020 bankruptcy, cited a [41% decline in consumer revenue](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOqzAUhlcDHchPDIWL26TLbadEZ-wD9sgPhE8SZfcjsoWpv1__6-u-3iGmWPb_kNHSVteCr5aQCM8VHvujUSxbAoq1XOSAA8-0CiamgS0DFys4ik9cFfTebogCZY-Wm3kRzGjN-2ARjZw1Qy44OOZBam_mDRV3G0ruoI_28mMLF5wxrZbRM1QwLbOZvPuWqDvF0Eeq5_hTY6GAW3rXJ56jq7lPNhAdrZP_OnHrxM3BeDUd3xBqvRSduGXnEpAL72F_UBsuftaa21A-y17R45BrodAGIZSRi9J8DJRTf1p_vGJKsU2mU2zPENMnlv741tOK3wAAAP__pc2Beg) over five years, reflecting an ongoing decline in newspaper advertising and readership, and came despite efforts by the company to cut costs and increase productivity by using AI content tools. _(Editor’s Note: As legacy media continues to struggle, The Flyover keeps expanding. We launched new state editions in_[ _Michigan_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz7GO6yAQheGnsbtEeDA4FBS3SZfbbokmMNizwmDZk0T79qtstf3W5-iT_o9buCEXrvN_XMlLbqHS6ygkQnvAx_w4hGsuKNzqe9lwo70EUGBPyp0GCBiFnxRG7JPPREC6Jz9MFwdqMmboF29BJ6PJRg04OTUksO5-ieByNtGi7dm_PeUGGJQyozsnRSNad5lsindNphsVJZa2nz8bV1kol6_2pP0c29oXv4hsR6f_dXDt4CoLrRwXnrH-unVw7XeftheXwoedulHNK3L5IeSP5U8P3wEAAP__x5Vujw) _and_[ _Pennsylvania_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzz1vwjAQxvFPY28gv8Z48NCFja4drQs5k6uMHSVHEN--olP3zs-jn_T_uuQLUKV2-4Q7Ji49N3xuFZlxzfC4PTamViow9fZeFlhwrdkoMxxUPGiT4cq0Y3Ygp1QQDVqJSYdTNCp4r-WcSlTFO-_DWKxxpwA6auuHMEbQow1eUnp7KmqjlfIuHieFDoZ4CsN0HS164RROxH09fndqPGOpr77jerz2u6xpZl42YT-EOQtz5hkXbG171R0awZ-rMGe5pml5Uq20DUE4dbsD1V-G_1m_J_MTAAD__0JXb9s) _just this month. ## US Map: Where People Stay Put
Louisiana may be losing population overall, but it tops a [new Census map](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU8DmZEpMODAwSZkvemGqBoXUCsDll2A5vajnitM_L_ek96_1_RCDnysf3EnJ8s5HfTkQCKUJrzWKwsfS0Dh8_gsESOlMIGGTmmraphwFr5parH0biECakpydT9Y0L0xdbk5MPUw2IF8_cZ-aNoFem2snY0xxvcIJbsPT9saaq1NayuvqcXODn3n53dDpmg1eZYzVf9PPmSjJXydN6VqPvcyuE0k5qL5U8BYwPg8T3VzvjDMGFkwcJbPsYBxxxjJK_RXkKwC33ysig8lG3FSb06yqSwoVMBYJufjwyFw7vqi1euOHH6E8stOt4PvAAAA___8Y38-) as the state with the most adult residents who were also born there, at 74% of the adult population. Michigan and Ohio follow at 72% and 71%, and the [2024 American Community Survey](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuszAQwPGnMVvQ-TAmDB7yfRVburRS1Qkd9kFcORjBQdS3r9JX6PyXfsP_49pfKaY4T690Zydj7md-bIlFeO1pn_ZN4jwmkpjnZ1lo4TX1CGhP0J409uQlHtwbKoIbmZGrgp1uzi1CU9e6uDkYjUeNaKk-D9COwQ_oK1s1phosDbqI7ulBq1ED1KYtA7Ah254bG_xQca0McIiS1_Irx1luPKbvfPBa-nwvkruJLJuqLgo7hV0godLzvO1bOeVDYSc0JFbYXf6_vbzrTwQ05T-wALpYXVgeMaW42UYZmO4U068qf5xxOPwJAAD___y3ck0) shows Midwest and Southern states dominating the top of the rankings, with Iowa, Wisconsin, and Mississippi all above 60% of its adult residents being native-born. Nevada ranks last at 17%, shaped by decades of rapid [population growth](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmZHpwQYCB5uQzaYboh7cQO96MLIb0Nx-xf9H-HE9Vanen-f4RA68Lb_xTU7mOG505UAilEY8liMLb3NA4bjdyY47pTCCBqt0r2oYcRI-aWyw9G4mAnqU5Oq260G3xtTl6gx0Hm0_kbbW2rqdyLYNTv4m5s6Ykt3dp_saaq1N01deU4O271rrp9eDTNFo8iwxVX8jb7LSHD7xpFRN8V0Gt4rsuXj8KmAoYLiuqzo5Hxgm3FkwcJYbLGBIuP0jrw6V1R734_uWWlK8ZFWvj8qCQqruW61AgylgKJPz-8UhcLZt0ejljRy-ZuWHtk4H_wMAAP__uiqAFg), adding many newcomers to the census. Florida comes in at just 26%, followed by Arizona at 30% and Colorado at 32%. Nationwide, 49% of U.S. adults still live in their birth state, with 35% of those who stayed citing family as the reason. You can [see where your state ranks here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU8DmZEpMODAwSZkvemGqBoXUCsDll2A5vajnitM_L_ek96_1_RCDnysf3EnJ8s5HfTkQCKUJrzWKwsfS0Dh8_gsESOlMIGGTmmraphwFr5parH0biECakpydT9Y0L0xdbk5MPUw2IF8_cZ-aNoFem2snY0xxvcIJbsPT9saaq1NayuvqcXODn3n53dDpmg1eZYzVf9PPmSjJXydN6VqPvcyuE0k5qL5U8BYwPg8T3VzvjDMGFkwcJbPsYBxxxjJK_RXkKwC33ysig8lG3FSb06yqSwoVMBYJufjwyFw7vqi1euOHH6E8stOt4PvAAAA___8Y38-).
| _Flying together with our sponsor_ [](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkbGO3CAQhp8Gd15hwGAKF5FO213alGgMw-4kGCw8t6e8fbSrREqVJu3M_N980v_tPbwDFaq3r7DjyrmFip9nQWbsAT5uHydTzQWYWn1uDjiwl6CksqP046QCRKYHBgNDWjOiQj3gOrnFK-nmeRru62JQo4ubM7NzSnrn_LxJnTdUUcrsBlqfPOknNUk5G39JEg1Yvzib4qZxFkZiIm798r1R5Tvm8rM9sF9i24ey3pmPU-gvQl2FunKH-OPPIRS-x1YzJaxMUJ4Joa5ympy1Ro9eRzWaKc2jj6hGWDBnr-UyzSD09SgQccfKQr_9fhnOo9Wz9bAD1fB0VlYoC4mS0G9765Xq7WTKWSjLr2GijpG38A9C-Ds49DUdn1QKndYJI2870Et84P9s6LGqXwEAAP__rUynkA) **Why Your Joints Feel So Stiff Every Morning (and Worse Every Year)** For decades, doctors blamed joint stiffness on cartilage loss and inflammation. But Harvard researchers discovered something different -- a hidden "drought" inside your joints that slowly drains the lubricating fluid they need to move freely. The odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week rose to 90% after the report. On Friday, the Labor Department said gasoline prices accounted for more than one-third of the monthly increase in the CPI report. Gasoline is up 27.4% from a year ago, although it increased 3.9% in August from the prior month. Meanwhile, on Friday, up 63% from a year ago. Because diesel powers the trucks and trains that move goods across the country, the surge is expected to ripple through consumer prices for months. Core prices, which strip out food and energy, jumped , also a bit higher than expected. Newspapers Hit by National Wave of Layoffs One of America's largest newspaper chains cut more than nationally across at least 13 papers Thursday, with some newsrooms losing up to 40% of their staff in McClatchy's most severe layoffs in years. The Fresno Bee was left with roughly a dozen reporters to cover California's fifth-largest city. The Miami Herald , which once employed 300 journalists, will now have . Papers in Idaho, Kansas City, Charlotte, and Kentucky were also hit. McClatchy, owned by hedge fund Chatham Asset Management since its 2020 bankruptcy, cited a over five years, reflecting an ongoing decline in newspaper advertising and readership, and came despite efforts by the company to cut costs and increase productivity by using AI content tools. ## Thune's PAC Drops $32 Million on Texas
Texas PAC, a new super PAC tied to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., purchased roughly $32 million in broadcast TV ads Friday supporting Republican [Ken Paxton's Senate campaign](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb9G3hRItF8SDRq6aHtdOxqUTcVEZMmw2Tjp1xc20C_oRoC4h4f313f_jZy5PH7iTF7eqfaF9i2TCK3nKCiUkNdU6yj0xi2iSA8Grto4baHHQfhFfYfN6KMZnW3I29vdgbXGds3k7-DSAMZR6wzcI3bXllLCKyVj3PhlGvYHzjh7RNrWXpy7xa9uuNk2tgBjUp2hkaWuF5nolEj5U1-0XoY6N9lPIsum2h8KgoKw7_vluaEcSwXheEJBOGMKwnFKQTBOQbBWQdiooJBeafkdMw9YNp24YM4fPdfImf-Q3lkmHfmh51roo1Nd9ZOKXvAttWgu-h-9Wf247Jwzb9eb6sxjRs6npfxvuy8PfwMAAP__TJSQQg) across four major Texas markets, according to tracking firm AdImpact. It marks Senate Republicans' first general-election money in Texas after [backing Sen. John Cornyn](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAUhJ8GOiP_cCEuXGxDl223RMfmGKw4GNknQN5-Ba9wu5FGM_Np_j3HJ4QY1vkvvNHQ6dO44lEiEmG-JQGhh5B9ShPhCcUC0Si57BjXTMgRHIUdxxbqyVg-aVGjEf1DSyG4aOvF-K7r7APhxyunQHqtWqW5BQGyfSgn6mCuOq7FFVFKNFr39qd1vVBWSTn5quU4BUq5oQVvCB-_acfcuPSuo1mItlKpP5UcKjkcx9H4dF7wl1_JYUsxUHClkkPG7WNjcLAyBzvE_GWQc9ixsBeubIOT0spsmJn9uFdh9xpL3uNawo4sbbgW5qAszMeUphkIS53NtB0hxlC6vmr5_IYQbzb67ae7kf8DAAD__3NSkOQ), R-Texas, in the primary. Paxton trails Democrat James Talarico in public polling and has been heavily outspent, though President Donald Trump's operation and Elon Musk's PAC have come online in recent weeks. Trump turned the [Dallas convention](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkT2O4zAMRk9jdwz05zgqXGyTbrbd0qAlKhYgS4LEZDK3XzhXmIosPj4-gv--1i-MKebHXzxo4Xcoa6bvnoiZ2qdlZAoYWyjFM72xb8i8KqGuICxItaLj-KLV4OiXTXgrR1rkfLNKSiHNuC_BbxN57wzO0yz01c-otZU3a9FRMGKMy4kTVp4jWsuLtfM2GTdLvWmlfBiMIB-5tAvv9JEI6ae8qF1cOca07My1D_rPoO6DuvNOFVvsp_0ZGNQd66DuGTmWjOmMtOdROzBhj_kBsQPvBLVFR1DxzSXDjh64QMWfszw7QaP63FJ0mOGInqkd4Ep-UT6xwOXc0zi6RKufDFppZ5jCTcE0GQKraQMRpnCjq9AC7WXnI41t8fU7phT7dR6MeBwY0-cq_u03Xov6HwAA___iHKG_) stage into a fundraiser for Paxton, praising him as "our greatest attorney general" between jabs at his looks. The new PAC plans to run ads continuously through Election Day.

body:
Here's the latest breaking news at The Maine Wire

** Trump Administration Exempts Canadian Road Salt and Cement from Upcoming Tariffs (https://us.list-manage.com/FMVySiYpKPn?e=f093fa355c&c2id=ed20d54774fd5b0d29c30444211870ed)
------------------------------------------------------------
By Libby Palanza on Sep 11, 2026 12:27 pm

name: Susan Collins
subject: This is my story
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Collins for Senator
body:
It all started in a small town in Aroostook County.
| Hi, it's Susan.I don't get to slow down and share this very often, so today I wanted to take a moment to tell you a bit about how I got here.I grew up in Caribou, Maine - one of six kids raised by my parents, Pat and Don. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. **I don't come from wealth or power. I come from humble beginnings.**

I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. clean_body: We’re back with campaign updates | | = Friend, It’s been a minute since our last campaign newsletter, but with 52 days to go until Election Day, we’re locked in and ready to run through the tape. Read on for campaign updates and how you can help us win on November 3rd. What We’ve Been Up To We’ve been busy this past week! Here’s a recap: Dan is trying to hide his record by saying he thinks data centers need local approval. Funny — last year he voted against every guardrail on data centers in the Big Beautiful Bill. Earlier this year, he was calling himself pro-data center at the Farm Show. Rachel’s said since day one: communities deserve a real say. Not because it's trending — because it's right. Now Dan's using her words because he feels the politics shifting. The bottom line: Dan Meuser isn't for local control. He's for Dan Meuser, and we need to make sure people know the truth ahead of Nov. 3. Last week we joined everyone who came out for the Walk for Recovery in Schuylkill Haven. People shared their stories, and the stories of people they love. And there were amazing service providers on hand to connect people to help. It was a wonderful reminder of the power of community — no one has to do this alone. We had a great time talking to the folks at the fire company and eating some great food -- shout out to the Welsh cakes from the Nicholson UMC! Last weekend at Hamburger Fest we got to see, taste, and experience some of the best our small businesses have to offer (and eat hamburgers, of course!). Hamburg continues to be a wonderful community, and that was clear last weekend. Schuylkill County Wine Fest: Our team had a great afternoon at the Schuylkill County Wine Fest celebrating our local wineries and supporting the gorgeous Hegins Park. Elysburg All Homes Day: You know the potato pancakes are good when the recipe is from someone’s grandma. The Overlook Fire Company served some good ones in Elysburg this weekend. Thanks to Commissioner Meghan Beck for joining us in talking to folks from Northumberland and Montour counties – including some wonderful artisans. ** Labor Day weekend, we celebrated workers in Luzerne County at the 5th annual NEPA-Que. It was a hit! : We were so grateful to the United Labor Council for inviting us to their Labor Day flag raising, and we’d like to thank them for everything they do for working families. Rachel spoke about the ongoing fight for worker protections and a higher minimum wage. Lebanon County Legislative Farm Tour: We heard concerns from our farmers in Lebanon County this week. About data centers. About our government undercutting our own with questionable beef imports. About tariffs that keep adding higher costs and uncertainty. Enough is enough — it’s time to stand with our farmers. If you have events in your area you’d like to invite Rachel to, please get in touch with us atmailto:info@wallaceforcongress.com. Upcoming Events and Volunteer Opportunities Every Tuesday until the election, 6-8PM: Join us from home or at the Pottsville office to make calls to voters across the district and get out the vote. September 12, 2-8PM = Join us for live music, drinks, food, and fun — and a chance to support our campaign. = September 17, 7-9PM: = Join Sharon Brumbaugh, Linda & Wayne Foxworth, Pat & Dan Hottenstein, and Kathie & Tom Teeter for a No Frills Fundraiser in Mt. Gretna! = September 21, 5-7PM: = Join Rachel for some of the best tacos in the district at Fourth Taco in Bloomsburg. We are asking for $100 to attend. body:
Are you proud to be an American citizen?

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGK2zAQhp9GvtlII9mxDz4UvIZCs9s2lB6FVho7A7KkWnJK-_QlJekD9DjzwzfM938_67MhT2F9NRuOlLN20WlLhX5jyFdKO_44aMd8o5W80cChq_lQC9DGFrqhVqZyYwuiX_oKR3HqBxCqHdrqOrYWDfT4Dp3tlhYlCrUI2yloDSwSlorGO48PAgRwKaDprGjV6b3H1i0OhGGKH8mZgg2FTA6zjTGl6KmQzU3c18qP11JSZvIDg5nBnNEeO7rmSt5nZzw26A4G87-Zwex-UVjrx5NMztkyOXHewfDKQcEndZ7eppeXC4PuKJvO8dgtMjmlPeaEtlBYH9GGjo6NyQk3Q_6xtGZLhtbA5PT30lPnM46hYChMTp-_vn2b9JdT_fFyqZ8mqn106Sd5T7k7McXXO7mxcavK__ZzG-FPAAAA___sUaIP)

| | Dear Fellow American, Are you proud to be an American citizen? If you’re like me, you give thanks to God every day that you live in a country that is free, peaceful, and where citizens have inalienable rights. Most people in history can’t say the same thing—in fact, most people in the world can’t say the same thing even today. You don’t have to be a historian to see that the long practice of citizenship in America is unprecedented. It’s one of our nation’s great achievements. But there’s a catch—citizenship requires vigilance and knowledge to maintain. Especially now, when it faces threats from the far-Left and progressive economic policies, illegal immigration, and more. Everyone who wishes to defend freedom in America requires an understanding of the nature and scope of these challenges. As a college, we know that a proper education is the best defense of liberty. And unlike the vast majority of colleges and universities, we must **reach** and **teach** millions of Americans about liberty. And we have to do it without taking ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of student grants and loans. NOT. ONE. PENNY—to remain proudly independent. This means that your support is critical to our success. With your help, we’ll engage the far-Left on the battlefield of education. With your help, we will defend liberty against dangerous ideologies. And with your help, we will preserve freedom for future generations of American citizens. You can give safely and securely at this link: [https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/dying-citizen](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGK2zAQhp9GvtlII9mxDz4UvIZCs9s2lB6FVho7A7KkWnJK-_QlJekD9DjzwzfM938_67MhT2F9NRuOlLN20WlLhX5jyFdKO_44aMd8o5W80cChq_lQC9DGFrqhVqZyYwuiX_oKR3HqBxCqHdrqOrYWDfT4Dp3tlhYlCrUI2yloDSwSlorGO48PAgRwKaDprGjV6b3H1i0OhGGKH8mZgg2FTA6zjTGl6KmQzU3c18qP11JSZvIDg5nBnNEeO7rmSt5nZzw26A4G87-Zwex-UVjrx5NMztkyOXHewfDKQcEndZ7eppeXC4PuKJvO8dgtMjmlPeaEtlBYH9GGjo6NyQk3Q_6xtGZLhtbA5PT30lPnM46hYChMTp-_vn2b9JdT_fFyqZ8mqn106Sd5T7k7McXXO7mxcavK__ZzG-FPAAAA___sUaIP) **And for a gift of $100 or more, you’ll receive a special hardcover edition of Victor Davis Hanson’s book,** **_The Dying Citizen: How Progressive Elites, Tribalism, and Globalization Are Destroying the Idea of America_****. Victor Davis Hanson is a frequent commentator on Fox News and online. He’s also a historian and distinguished fellow here at Hillsdale.** Regarding the book, my boss and teacher, Hillsdale President Larry P. Arnn, has written, “In this book, Hanson demonstrates yet again his command across time and for our time. **This book and he are a treasure.** ” Thank you so much for your partnership in promoting the kind of intelligent patriotism—especially among younger Americans—that is essential to preserving citizenship and free government.
---
| | Warm regards, Bill Gray, ’01
Vice President
National Donor Outreach
Hillsdale College
