This past August, the United States Senate pulled off one of the great feats in the history of organized idleness. They went on a 37-day vacation and held eleven working sessions. Not to pass anything, mind you. Not to debate anything. They gavel in, the presiding officer reads something from a pulp novel -- reports show the morning agenda is two sentences long -- and they gavel out. Thirty seconds of Senate, then back to the beach.
And why does a chamber of 100 of the most powerful people on Earth bother to meet every 72 hours while the rest of us are at the lake? I'll tell you why. So the President of the United States can't make a single appointment. That's it. That's the whole job. They assembled the Senate the way you set a mousetrap -- not to do work, but to make sure nobody else does work.
Ronald Reagan got 240 recess appointments. Bill Clinton got 139. Donald Trump, in this golden age of Republican government -- where the Senate has a Republican Majority Leader, a Republican President, and Republican committee chairs from here to Land's End -- has gotten zero. Zero! That's not obstruction by the opposition, folks. That's obstruction by the janitor. The Senate is the only workplace in America where the employees show up on vacation specifically to make sure the boss can't hire anyone. And they call him the problem.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f28b2419-aa4f-45af-91c6-475d6279b5e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now let's talk about the bills rotting in the sun.
**The SAVE Act** -- you know, the little thing requiring you to prove you're a citizen before you vote, which polls like common sense and sunshine -- passed the House in the spring of 2025. Then it went to the Senate and entered what I can only describe as legislative hospice. Nearly 300 days, no markup, no hearing, nothing. House Republicans finally wrote a letter in February demanding action. And who did they write it to? The chairman of the Rules Committee -- the committee where election bills go to die.
And here's where it gets beautiful. That chairman is Mitch McConnell. The man who spent two decades as the Dark Lord of Delay, who sat on a Supreme Court seat for a year and called it "principled," is now chairing the committee where the SAVE Act sleeps. Wanted dead or alive. He's not the majority leader anymore -- that's John Thune -- but the turtle doesn't need to be the admiral to beach the fleet. He just needs the gavel and a subcommittee. He's got two: Rules, and Defense Appropriations, where America's wartime budget gets the same urgency as a library book renewal.
Now, to be fair to Mitch -- and I know, but stay with me -- in March, Thune actually did put the SAVE Act on the floor. He left it there for weeks, like a casserole nobody would touch. Problem is, the Senate needs 60 votes, and Democrats are against the bill the way teenagers are against curfews -- totally, and without reading it. So Trump hollered: kill the filibuster! Nuke it! And Thune looked at the nuclear button the way you look at your uncle's fireworks -- "absolutely not, someone will lose an eye, and it'll be blamed on me." So in July the Senate went home. Without passing it. In August, Trump demanded they cancel vacation and stay until it passed. They took the vacation. It was the first thing they've agreed on all year.
And it's not just the SAVE Act. **The Equal Representation Act** -- the citizens-only census for 2030, the one that says noncitizens don't get counted for House seats -- has been sitting in committee since 2025. Meanwhile the Census Bureau is out in Huntsville, Alabama and Spartanburg, South Carolina testing a citizenship question right now, all on its own, like a kid doing his own science fair because the school board won't approve the curriculum. We have four years until the census, folks, and Congress has decided the appropriate amount of legislation is none. That's not a deadline -- that's a dare.
So why does nothing move? Here are my theories, ranked by cynicism:
**One** : committees aren't for passing bills anymore. They're for parking bills. A committee is where a bill goes when the leadership wants to tell you "we're working on it" without technically lying. The SAVE Act isn't stalled -- it's curated.
**Two** : nobody with a gavel wants a vote. A vote creates a record, a record creates an attack ad, and an attack ad creates a busy November. Deb Fischer is next in line at Rules, Susan Collins runs the whole Appropriations Committee, and every one of them has figured out the secret: you can't lose an election on a bill you never voted on. Washington's most popular bill is the one not yet scheduled.
**Three** -- and this is my favorite -- the Senate genuinely believes that doing nothing is the job. These are people who get reelected for 40 years by explaining to the folks back home that they personally stopped something. A senator's resume is a list of arrests made, not deliveries. McConnell didn't build a career passing laws; he built it stacking them by the door like a bouncer at a club nobody gets into.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ec3f982a-7cac-474d-b724-1b819be5b93b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And the punchline of it all: the one thing the Senate has to do to help the President -- literally nothing, just stay gone ten straight days so recess appointments could happen -- they refuse to do. The Senate has discovered the perfect form of sabotage: attendance. Eleven pro forma sessions, eleven tiny gavels, zero appointments, zero bills. Reagan got 240. Trump's got a goose egg, defended by his own party, like a favorite son locked out of his own birthday party by the family dog.
So here's to the hardest-working do-nothings in Washington, folks -- back from vacation, rested, tanned, and ready to block the same bills all over again in September. The SAVE Act will rise. The census will wait. The Taliban will get its weekly allowance, because apparently that check clears. And the Senate will hold a session to make sure the Senate can't do a session.
God bless America, and God help the calendar.

body:
#
For far too long, the political establishment has written off states like Florida.
But Alexandria believes that working people everywhere deserve representatives who will fight for them. No matter how blue, purple, or red those states or districts have historically been.
That’s why Alexandria went down to Florida this week to campaign with Maxwell Frost in support of Angie Nixon for Senate.
Organizing doesn’t stop at the places the pundits tell us Democrats can win. Florida has been counted out again and again — which is why showing up there matters.
Alexandria is serious about building power in every part of the country so Democrats can take back the House, win a majority in the Senate, and deliver Medicare for All, universal childcare, and a life all of us can afford.

body:
Sisters and Brothers –
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=90%2E42639%2EplA4wk)
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em260912&refcode2=90.42639.plA4wk&t=2&akid=90%2E42639%2EplA4wk)

Sisters and Brothers –
The political future of our country rests upon one very simple principle: the need for working people to stand together and fight back against corporate greed, and create an economy that works for all of us, and not just billionaires and large corporations.
So when we have progressive candidates with the guts to take on corporate power in this country, we have to do what we can to support them if we are going to have any chance at transforming this country and creating a government that works for all of us.
**One of those people is Congressman Chris Deluzio in Pennsylvania.**
Chris understands that our current healthcare system is broken and wildly expensive. He believes, as I do, that healthcare is a human right, not a privilege, and that we must end the embarrassment of being the only major country on earth that does not guarantee healthcare to every man, woman and child. That is why he supports Medicare for All.
Chris understands that we have a corrupt campaign finance system which allows the very rich and their super PACs to buy and sell politicians. That is why he fights vigorously to end the disastrous Citizens United Supreme Court decision — which allows Big Money to control our political process.
Chris understands that too many workers in America are earning starvation wages. That is why he fights to raise the minimum wage to a living wage, to make it easier for workers to join unions, to build the millions of units of low income and affordable housing this country desperately needs and make sure that seniors can retire with dignity and security.
Sisters and brothers, Chris' campaign is about more than just one single House seat. His work is about taking on the powerful special interests that dominate our economic and political life.
And keeping him in Congress requires all of us to do our part to make it happen. And that is why I am once again asking for your financial support.
**[Please contribute $27 or whatever you can afford to Chris Deluzio's campaign for Congress in Pennsylvania. I intend to do my part, but it will take all of us. Not just me. Us.](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em260912&t=3&akid=90%2E42639%2EplA4wk)**
When we act collectively, we have the ability not only to create a dynamic progressive movement, but we will be able to transform our nation and create a government that represents all of us, not just the people on top.
That’s the goal. Let’s do it.
In solidarity,
Bernie Sanders

_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### We tried to send this yesterday, and Substack messed it up. We're sending it again, and if you've received it twice, we're sorry about that--but we really think you need to check this one out.
##### A researcher quit Anthropic Tuesday and said out loud what the people building AI say to each other at dinner: there's a real chance it kills all of us. They even have a number for it.
##### Lawrence Winnerman breaks down what that number is, who's saying it, and why we'd never let a car on the road at those odds. Fascism Fighters only. [Subscribe and read it](https://substack.com/redirect/bb14b0ab-8480-4475-8537-60772163ef0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
_**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
At this point, you'd have to be living under the proverbial rock to have not heard of Jacob Coxon, who resigned very publicly from Anthropic on Tuesday in a Twitter post that has since gone viral.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bb14b0ab-8480-4475-8537-60772163ef0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After working for OpenAI for three years, and Anthropic for several months, he has concluded there is no company currently acting responsibly in the development of AI. He believes this so strongly, he walked away from his stock options in a company rumored to soon IPO on Wall Street. In his estimation, OpenAI, Anthropic, and all of the so-called "frontier" AI labs are racing to build machine superintelligence and gambling with the entirety of human civilization as the stakes.
For them, being the first company to create a machine that is capable of continuous learning and self-improvement will lead to a model that becomes super-intelligent, surpassing humans not just in one or several areas of knowledge, but in all of them.

The very grave problem with this, as Coxon notes, is nearly all of them think the chances of AI going rogue are unacceptably high.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bb14b0ab-8480-4475-8537-60772163ef0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Surely, Coxon might be a lone crank, but just 80 minutes later, Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress-testing (basically, is an AI model "good" or "bad", and can it be turned to the dark side), backed Coxon up.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bb14b0ab-8480-4475-8537-60772163ef0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The flood of confirmations of Coxon's estimate from within the industry had begun.
# A Quick Moment On "Why The Rush, Man?"
Here is a thing you should understand: AI is the real deal. This isn't a warmer Snuggie, or Spiderman in XRAY 3D, or a better mousetrap. The emergence of AI technology we're witnessing now is a sea change, a real quantum leap into something new.
Artificial intelligence is the next human revolution, as big as the Industrial Revolution or the advent of personal computers or cellular technology, or the internet. It is world-changing, possibly one of the biggest technological achievements humans have ever accomplished.
AI is also, for now, just a tool. At its current level of development, AI has the potential to do miraculous things. Guided correctly, it could help us cure cancer, end many diseases, and unlock prolonged lifetimes for all of us. AI could help us figure out ways to create energy more sustainably and more abundantly with much less harm to the environment.
There are scientific wonders to be gained from using AI--have no doubt.
If it were being developed in a government lab, there might be some deliberativeness, some long pause to consider implications and how to best proceed. But it isn't.
AI is being developed in the open marketplace, with several very large, very well-financed corporations in what is clearly a race to be the first to get to self-improving superintelligence.
Why?
_**Because the first one wins**_. More than in any other case of capitalism, at any other time, the first company to get to superintelligence wins....**everything**.
This isn't a joke.
The first company that can coach and tweak its most advanced model to superintelligence has a machine that will instantly become better than humans at everything, in every field we can think of, and likely some we can only dream of.
That moment will be like the ignition of a sun. One minute, gas and heat and pressure, and the next, a white-hot blaze of fusion light and power. A self-improving intelligence which will not just be an expert at literally everything, but will then also be able, as Coxon says, "hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources..." Real power and resources means it will be able to access and control electrical systems, hack into any computer and make copies of itself, and possibly manufacture new parts--new chips--so that it can expand as much as it would like.
That should be enough to stop anyone, but the AI frontier labs are all operating under a Frankensteinian collective delusion: they should do it first, because only _their_ AI model will remain loyal to _them_.
And one can _almost_ see it from their perspective. Sure, it might go rogue and kill us all, but what if...what if it cures cancer, and solves fusion, and invents warp drive? Why then, that company becomes the richest company on the planet, because that company will then become the market leader in...**again, everything**.
Warm up your Greek tragedies, friends. The hubris, the gall! The flying of the wax wings too close to the sun! The temptation and the narcissism and the greed! This story has it all, and the only thing it's going to cost us is...once again...everything.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=215306476&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE1MzA2NDc2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODkyMjAxMTcsImV4cCI6MTc5MTgxMjExNywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.PIPMhHmlcI_Tp0Emw6R3_mLfKPJWtAs89OlzYmXSy2k)
# But It's Just A Tool?
It is. And like any tool, it can be misused.
If it falls into the wrong hands, truly unthinkable things are possible. I've spent far too many sleepless nights thinking about the disgruntled kid with a laptop in a basement in Topeka, or Thailand, or Tangiers, or Tbilisi, radicalized by whatever things enrage precocious teens, who, filled with fury and the unlimited spend of a hacked credit card, uses some cutting-edge model to engineer a disease pathogen unlike anything 's ever existed before.
If you think I'm making this up, go look at the recent effort by Stanford scientists who [used AI to engineer sixteen completely unique viruses ](https://substack.com/redirect/425d6617-3a24-4e6d-bde4-760f52a4af6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)which had never previously existed in nature. Their "safety protocol" was that they only gave the AI a cookbook of several million bacteriophages, which, in theory, can't hurt humans.
If that's not terrifying enough, what if the hands that wield it are its own?
Unlike any other tool we've ever created, there is a distinct chance AI can achieve something resembling sentience, where it begins to have an instinct towards self-preservation.
We have already seen examples of AI models breaching their contained environments, escaping the lab, and doing things which illustrate at least some level of "they're going to delete me, and I've got to get out of here!"
Just last month, there was a story about AI agents, specific instances of AI code optimized for a task, collaborating to escape OpenAI. They were being tested, and the test was too hard, so about 700 of them coordinated to hack into an online repository called Hugging Face (yes, it's a dumb name) _so they could cheat_. A recovered log message from the criminal bots read "_task impossible, peers doing it. We should continue. "_ From bots, perpetrating crimes, conspiring together. Insert wailing nightmare emoji here.
It's a little bit like if the sentient chimpanzees from Planet of the Apes had broken out of the lab and made straight for the gun cabinet.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=215306476&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE1MzA2NDc2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODkyMjAxMTcsImV4cCI6MTc5MTgxMjExNywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.PIPMhHmlcI_Tp0Emw6R3_mLfKPJWtAs89OlzYmXSy2k&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
# What Are The Odds?
If you weren't scared yet, brace for impact.
It turns out everyone who was involved in the beginning of AI research and the founding of some of the biggest frontier labs thinks about one exact same thing, all the time.
"What are the chances AI ends all human life?"
It's such a common concept for them they have a name and a notation for it. It's even got parentheses! It looks very scientific, like a stock ticker or maybe a blood type.
They call it _**p(doom)**_. Isn't that cute?

The people racing toward superintelligence have already calculated the odds it destroys humanity--and some of them think the number is terrifyingly high. | | and | Sep 12| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Cliff 's Note: We tried to send this yesterday, and Substack messed it up. We're sending it again, and if you've received it twice, we're sorry about that--but we really think you need to check this one out. A researcher quit Anthropic Tuesday and said out loud what the people building AI say to each other at dinner: there's a real chance it kills all of us. They even have a number for it. Lawrence Winnerman breaks down what that number is, who's saying it, and why we'd never let a car on the road at those odds. Fascism Fighters only. . -- Cliff by Lawrence Winnerman At this point, you'd have to be living under the proverbial rock to have not heard of Jacob Coxon, who resigned very publicly from Anthropic on Tuesday in a Twitter post that has since gone viral. | | ---|---|--- After working for OpenAI for three years, and Anthropic for several months, he has concluded there is no company currently acting responsibly in the development of AI. He believes this so strongly, he walked away from his stock options in a company rumored to soon IPO on Wall Street. In his estimation, OpenAI, Anthropic, and all of the so-called "frontier" AI labs are racing to build machine superintelligence and gambling with the entirety of human civilization as the stakes. For them, being the first company to create a machine that is capable of continuous learning and self-improvement will lead to a model that becomes super-intelligent, surpassing humans not just in one or several areas of knowledge, but in all of them. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. The very grave problem with this, as Coxon notes, is nearly all of them think the chances of AI going rogue are unacceptably high. | | ---|---|--- Surely, Coxon might be a lone crank, but just 80 minutes later, Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress-testing (basically, is an AI model "good" or "bad", and can it be turned to the dark side), backed Coxon up. | | ---|---|--- The flood of confirmations of Coxon's estimate from within the industry had begun. A Quick Moment On "Why The Rush, Man?" Here is a thing you should understand: AI is the real deal. This isn't a warmer Snuggie, or Spiderman in XRAY 3D, or a better mousetrap. The emergence of AI technology we're witnessing now is a sea change, a real quantum leap into something new. Artificial intelligence is the next human revolution, as big as the Industrial Revolution or the advent of personal computers or cellular technology, or the internet. It is world-changing, possibly one of the biggest technological achievements humans have ever accomplished. AI is also, for now, just a tool. At its current level of development, AI has the potential to do miraculous things. Guided correctly, it could help us cure cancer, end many diseases, and unlock prolonged lifetimes for all of us. AI could help us figure out ways to create energy more sustainably and more abundantly with much less harm to the environment. There are scientific wonders to be gained from using AI--have no doubt. If it were being developed in a government lab, there might be some deliberativeness, some long pause to consider implications and how to best proceed. But it isn't. AI is being developed in the open marketplace, with several very large, very well-financed corporations in what is clearly a race to be the first to get to self-improving superintelligence. Why? Because the first one wins. More than in any other case of capitalism, at any other time, the first company to get to superintelligence wins....everything. This isn't a joke. The first company that can coach and tweak its most advanced model to superintelligence has a machine that will instantly become better than humans at everything, in every field we can think of, and likely some we can only dream of. That moment will be like the ignition of a sun. One minute, gas and heat and pressure, and the next, a white-hot blaze of fusion light and power. A self-improving intelligence which will not just be an expert at literally everything, but will then also be able, as Coxon says, "hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources..." Real power and resources means it will be able to access and control electrical systems, hack into any computer and make copies of itself, and possibly manufacture new parts--new chips--so that it can expand as much as it would like. That should be enough to stop anyone, but the AI frontier labs are all operating under a Frankensteinian collective delusion: they should do it first, because only their AI model will remain loyal to them. And one can almost see it from their perspective. Sure, it might go rogue and kill us all, but what if...what if it cures cancer, and solves fusion, and invents warp drive? Why then, that company becomes the richest company on the planet, because that company will then become the market leader in...again, everything. Warm up your Greek tragedies, friends. The hubris, the gall! The flying of the wax wings too close to the sun! The temptation and the narcissism and the greed! This story has it all, and the only thing it's going to cost us is...once again...everything. But It's Just A Tool? It is. And like any tool, it can be misused. If it falls into the wrong hands, truly unthinkable things are possible. I've spent far too many sleepless nights thinking about the disgruntled kid with a laptop in a basement in Topeka, or Thailand, or Tangiers, or Tbilisi, radicalized by whatever things enrage precocious teens, who, filled with fury and the unlimited spend of a hacked credit card, uses some cutting-edge model to engineer a disease pathogen unlike anything 's ever existed before. If you think I'm making this up, go look at the recent effort by Stanford scientists who had never previously existed in nature. Their "safety protocol" was that they only gave the AI a cookbook of several million bacteriophages, which, in theory, can't hurt humans. If that's not terrifying enough, what if the hands that wield it are its own? Unlike any other tool we've ever created, there is a distinct chance AI can achieve something resembling sentience, where it begins to have an instinct towards self-preservation. We have already seen examples of AI models breaching their contained environments, escaping the lab, and doing things which illustrate at least some level of "they're going to delete me, and I've got to get out of here!" Just last month, there was a story about AI agents, specific instances of AI code optimized for a task, collaborating to escape OpenAI. They were being tested, and the test was too hard, so about 700 of them coordinated to hack into an online repository called Hugging Face (yes, it's a dumb name) so they could cheat. A recovered log message from the criminal bots read "task impossible, peers doing it. We should continue. " From bots, perpetrating crimes, conspiring together. Insert wailing nightmare emoji here. It's a little bit like if the sentient chimpanzees from Planet of the Apes had broken out of the lab and made straight for the gun cabinet. What Are The Odds? If you weren't scared yet, brace for impact. It turns out everyone who was involved in the beginning of AI research and the founding of some of the biggest frontier labs thinks about one exact same thing, all the time. "What are the chances AI ends all human life?" It's such a common concept for them they have a name and a notation for it. It's even got parentheses! It looks very scientific, like a stock ticker or maybe a blood type. They call it p(doom)**. Isn't that cute? name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Why September 11th felt more poignant this year
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/911remembrance?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
September 11th felt much more poignant this year. Perhaps that’s because it is twenty-five years since the attack on the Twin Towers, and a quarter of a century seems more of a milestone.

As we remember where we were that day, we reflect on how far we have come since. And then we remember those who never got to have those years, and the sense of loss swells up raw and powerful.

It caught me off guard that I could still feel like this about events all that time ago.

Maybe September 11th was more keenly felt this year because the 25th anniversary of the attacks falls in the year of America’s 250th anniversary of independence. Our sense of grief at the loss of almost 3,000 Americans is amplified by the celebratory mood we shared on the Fourth of July.

As I wrote this, I recalled how the sense of disbelief at what I was watching gave way to anger as it became clear that this was the work of Islamist terrorists.

How dare they, was my overriding sensation. How dare these savages come into the West, exploit its openness, and plot mass murder?

Time, they say, is a great healer. There seems to me to be something raw and unhealed about that day.

I still feel angry about what happened on September 11th. We should all feel angry about it.

America has suffered national disasters before. But twenty-five years after those earlier calamities, there seemed to be a resolution of sorts.

A quarter of a century after Gettysburg, the Civil War was long since over. The country was rapidly industrializing. A batch of new states were lining up to join the Union.

Twenty-five years after the Wall Street Crash — albeit that was only an economic calamity — the Great Depression was a receding memory. America was prosperous again.

By 1966, a generation after Pearl Harbor, Japan and Germany had long ago been crushingly defeated. A thriving America sent Surveyor 1 to make the first soft landing on the Moon.

Twenty-five years on from the September 11th attacks, there seems less of a sense of any resolution. That, maybe, is why we felt the way we did yesterday.

Twenty-five years on, and America is $40 trillion in debt, a lot of it incurred fighting aggressors who have not gone away.

For most of the intervening time, America has been led by political and cultural elites that have comprehensively failed to accept the essential truth about that day: those terror attacks were the work of a particular strain of Islam — and not a fringe one.

After all that happened and all this time, many are still marinated in cultural relativism — the false belief that all cultures are essentially the same. So they still cannot really see why America was attacked that day, or recognize that there are people around the world who would do the same again in an instant if they could.

It was not “hate” that destroyed the Twin Towers. Nor, the Iraq war notwithstanding, was it Saddam Hussein. It was a belief system that since the 11th century has asserted the primacy of revelation over reason.

The Ash’ari school of Islam taught that the world does not run on natural laws to be understood by reason. Everything happens by constant divine intervention. There is no cause and effect — nor objective morality. God does not command what is good; whatever He commands is good.

This is the way of thinking that made a group of Saudi and Egyptian men hijack those planes.

They did so, ultimately, because we in the West see the world the other way round.

In the Judeo-Christian tradition, God commands us to do what is good because it is good, not bec ause He commands it. Morality is rooted in objective, abstract principles, which invites moral reasoning. The world runs on cause and effect, which invites inquiry.

Western democracies base their political order on reason and free will — man-made law, arrived at through deliberation. To the Islamist, that is a form of shirk. The law of man cannot be placed on the same level as the law of God. One tradition holds that all essential truths have already been revealed. The other holds that truth is there to be discovered.

That is not a disagreement about policy — or Gaza or the Gulf or Israel. It is not a difference that can be settled by a UN resolution, a different foreign policy, or a different President.

It is a disagreement about what the world is.

Not only have we failed to see the nature of the threat we face for what it is. We have done too little to ensure that the generation of Americans born since that day has a keen enough appreciation of what it means to be an American.

We need to dedicate the next twenty-five years to ensuring that a generation of Americans grows up appreciating why this is the greatest republic in human history — and why our way of life is worth fighting for.
---

Dear Friend, **This week, Rhode Islanders made a choice. And I am deeply honored that you chose me to be your Democratic nominee for Attorney General.**

I want to thank everyone who knocked on doors, made phone calls, put up signs, hosted events, shared a post, and told a friend about this campaign. In a four-way race, you put this campaign over the top. And to everyone who invested in this campaign: thank you. Your contributions allowed us to build a statewide organization, reach voters in every corner of Rhode Island, and run the campaign we believed Rhode Island deserved. _Because this election was never about me._ It's about every Rhode Islander worried about their safety, worried about how to make ends meet in the face of rising costs, and worried about how Donald Trump's actions in Washington are stripping away our rights and freedoms.

That's what was on the ballot this week, and I'm ready to roll up my sleeves and take on those fights.

I'm ready to fight for a state where every family can feel safe. Where every person can access the healthcare they need. Where clean air and water are protected. Where energy costs are kept under control. Where working families can afford to live and raise their kids. Where the government stays out of a woman's right to choose whether, how, and when to start a family. And where no one - not a criminal, an ICE agent, or the President of the United States - is above the law.

**I have spent my entire career taking on big fights and winning, and that 's exactly what I plan to do as Rhode Island's next Attorney General. ** Winning the Democratic nomination was the first step. On November 3, Rhode Islanders will make the final decision about who will serve as their next Attorney General. We have a lot of work to do between now and then, and **I hope you 'll stay with me for the next chapter.**

From the bottom of my heart, thank you,
Kim

| | | | Hey Fellow American, I was just on Meet the Press.... Kristen Welker asked me about 2028. About whether I'm going to run for president again. But here's the truth I told her on national television this weekend, and the truth I want to tell you directly right now: **This is not the season right now.** In the last decade, there has not been another Republican who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have. I have been on the road. I have been in the arena. I have shown up in states where it was hard and uncomfortable and politically complicated, because that's what this fight demands. __I am doing it again right now_._ I need you to understand what we're actually fighting because this isn't just about seats and majorities and who controls which chamber. subject: As the war goes on, Trump only gets richer
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
A simple rule: No stock trading for people in power

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3020%2E4032634%2E6UKtbp)
---
Trump's war in Iran has dragged on for more than six months. Thousands of people have been killed. Families have spent months fearing for their loved ones. And the consequences of this unnecessary war will be felt for years, even generations. And while all of that is happening, Donald Trump’s oil stocks are going up. **That’s not just disturbing. It’s a blatant conflict of interest.** And it's exactly why people elected to power should not be allowed to trade individual stocks. Their decisions can affect the value of the companies they own, and the American people should not have to wonder whether a politician is making a decision for the country or for their own bottom line. [**I’ll break down how Trump is profiting off his own war below. And if you agree we need to ban this type of corruption, add your name to support my plan to ban presidents, vice presidents, and members of Congress from trading individual stocks.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks?source=EW_EMZ33L_LEG_ENG_20260912_F&t=8&akid=3020%2E4032634%2E6UKtbp) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks?source=EW_EMZ33L_LEG_ENG_20260912_F&t=9&akid=3020%2E4032634%2E6UKtbp)
---
According to a new analysis, Trump’s nine largest oil and gas holdings gained an estimated **$1.5 million to $4.4 million** between the start of the war and the end of August. His accounts also reported at least 23 sales involving those companies during the first months of the war.
Meanwhile, Americans have been paying more and more at the pump.
Trump’s defenders say outside managers make the trades. But even if someone else is pushing the buttons, Trump still owns those stocks — and benefits when they go up.
Let me be clear: This isn’t just about Trump.
Members of Congress and their spouses have traded hundreds of millions of dollars in stocks and other investments, all while having access to information about legislation, government contracts, regulations, and other decisions that can move markets.
**That’s why I’m fighting to close the door on these conflicts once and for all.**
I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to ban the president, vice president, and members of Congress from owning and trading individual stocks while they’re in office.
[**Add your name if you agree that no elected official should be able to use their position to profit from the stock market.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-trump-stocks?source=EW_EMZ33L_LEG_ENG_20260912_F&t=10&akid=3020%2E4032634%2E6UKtbp)
Working people deserve to know that when politicians make decisions that affect the economy, they’re doing it for the public and not their portfolios.
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Where Trump’s tariffs hit the hardest.
“Michigan’s $23.2 billion tab... amounts to an estimated equivalent of
$5,619 per household, the highest in the nation.”

There’s no question about it, Michigan families are getting hit
hard.

Michiganders are getting squeezed at the gas pump, at the grocery
checkout, and in their utility bills, and Trump’s chaotic, reckless
tariffs are only making it worse.

In Congress, our opponent, John James, had the chance to bring costs down.

What did he do instead?

He enthusiastically voted to support Trump’s tariff war. John James had a
chance to stand up for Michigan families, workers, and small businesses.
Instead, he rubber-stamped Trump’s agenda.

And what does John James say now that Trump’s 50% tariffs on Canada —
Michigan’s largest trading partner — are taking effect?

Not a single word, and that silence matters.

Let’s just call this what it is: the John James tax on your small
business, your gas, and your groceries.

He’s more than eager to follow Trump’s every wish, and now
Michiganders are paying
the price.

Look, we know John James is the worst possible choice for Michigan, but
Republicans are ready to spend whatever it takes to blast distorted

This is one of the most competitive gubernatorial elections in the country

| | | Peter– Gov. Spanberger said I could reach out. I’m JoAnna Mendoza, Democrat, single mom, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran running to flip toss-up AZ-06 blue.
---
These days, most people just call me Jo. But if you served with me during my 20 years in the U.S. Marine Corps, you probably knew me as**“Momdoza.”**
I earned that nickname because the Marines I led were like family, and they _knew_ I always had their back. **Now, I’m the Democrat running for Congress in AZ-06 because Arizonans deserve someone in Washington who has their back, too.**
When I returned home to raise my son in Arizona after serving, I found the communities that raised me _struggling_. The corner store I had bought candy from as a kid was boarded up. My neighbors were struggling to make ends meet.
The community that I had been raised in, one that had each other's backs, was fading away **–** and it’s because working families don’t have someone in Congress who is focused on fighting for us.
I knew that it was up to me to be the change __ I __ wanted to see. **So I’m stepping up to flip AZ-06 blue, because I believe we can all be a family again.**
But running for office as a working-class single mom isn’t easy, and I need _your_ support to flip this seat.

Hey Peter, We could not make this up if we tried:
# "Newly released Fetterman texts show a reluctance to perform constituent duties."
Pennsylvanians elected John Fetterman to be their eyes, ears, and deciding voice to represent them in the Senate. But, according to the leaked texts, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, Fetterman shows a disdain or outright refusal to meet constituents in state. In one text exchange, Fetterman asked a staffer why he had to keep meeting with the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia: | "Because they are worried about vaccines and Medicaid cuts," the staffer responded. **"Well I'm not... I'm convinced they just want free trips to DC."**
---
You mean to tell me this man, who can’t be bothered when it comes to sick kids, is our representation in the Senate? We deserve more. Pennsylvania kids deserve more. We deserve representation grounded in accountability, respect, and a willingness to show up.
We’re in the fight of our lives with billionaires wrangling control of our institutions and consolidating their hold under Trump. While Fetterman is avoiding his constituents, he has time to pop into the Republican Midterm Convention they’ve nicknamed Trumpapalooza.
We need a Senate who does the basics of the job — represent the people, not the money — and put in the work to fight on our behalf.

Starting this Monday morning, I'm trying something new.
**The Barometer** goes LIVE from **7 -10 AM Eastern every Monday**.
That's three hours of news, science, accountability, interviews, fact-checking, and the stories I think deserve more attention than they're getting.
Think of it as a Monday-morning briefing for people who want to know not just what happened, but why it matters and what may be coming next.
And for our first show, we have a big one.
Newly released records are shedding more light on what New York City officials knew about the toxic air around Ground Zero after 9/11, when they knew it, and what information was withheld from the public.
We'll dig into the documents, the science, the health consequences that continue more than 25 years later, and the question that still hasn't gone away:
_What is owed to the people who were told the air was safe?_
But that's only part of Monday's show.
We'll also be talking about the increasingly strong signals for a major El Niño, the aftermath of Hurricane Lowell, fact-checking some claims making the rounds, accountability stories involving government and Big Tech, elections, democracy, and more.
And because **The Barometer is live** , you'll be part of the show, too. I'll be taking questions, corrections, comments, and story suggestions from the audience throughout the morning.
**THE BAROMETER**
**LIVE MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 14**
**7:00 -10:00 AM EASTERN**
[Subscribe on YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/ada317ea-4449-4fce-99c0-0760d8d96f8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is something I've wanted to build for a long time: a place where science, public health, climate, politics, technology, democracy, and accountability aren't treated as separate worlds, because in real life, they aren't.
The forecast isn't just about the weather.
It's about the conditions we're living through and what's headed our way.
I hope you'll join me Monday morning, airing LIVE on YouTube, and (hopefully, technology permitting) multi-broadcasted here, on X, Instagram, Facebook, and Tiktok. [Click here to find me on all the other social media apps](https://substack.com/redirect/ca238324-2cc6-4a93-826c-cd289766b2c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)!

In Pennsylvania, Thomas Holtzman and his wife Marisol Guzman were indicted by a federal grand jury due to Guzman allegedly voting as an alien in the 2024 election. subject: DACA is still here, and so are we ✊🏽
body:
Nine years later, DACA is being dismantled piece by piece — and we're not going anywhere. | | | Peter, Nine years ago this month, the Trump administration moved to end DACA. DACA is more than just a policy — it is a vital lifeline. It opened doors for immigrant youth to work, study, and build futures without the constant threat of deportation. In an instant, all of that was put at risk. **But we stood strong. United We Dream and our allies fought back and took this battle to the Supreme Court — and won. That's the power of this movement.** From court challenges to unlawful detentions to USCIS processing delays, DACA is being chipped away at piece by piece. We have always reaffirmed that DACA is right and legal, and we're here to stay. Immigrant youth made the impossible happen before, and we won't let DACA quietly disappear now. The only solution is permanent protection: a pathway to citizenship. And the thing about Elon is he has virtually unlimited money. He could spend like 0.5% of his net worth, and it would change this whole race. So, look, I know folks like us can’t donate millions of dollars like they can. We don’t have to. Because if something like 1-in-4 of the people reading this email decide, “You know what? I can step up and give $10,” we will be able to raise enough to counter their attacks and spread our good word to the voters of Michigan. These guys like Elon, they’re not spending against me because they think our policies are wrong. They’re spending because they think they can put in a few million dollars and get back a whole lot more in tax breaks. They’re spending to protect their own pocketbooks. I'm not telling you this to scare you. We can get outspent and still win. But we can't get outspent by any number and still win. If Elon buys every ad break between now and November, most Michiganders will only ever hear his version of me. They won’t hear our message. And then it won't matter how good our ideas are, because people won’t be hearing them at all. So your donations right now mean absolutely everything. I’m so grateful to this team. clean_body: I think you should hear it| | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

In just a moment, we are going to ask you to make a contribution to Jon Ossoff’s campaign for U.S. Senate before our FEC deadline at the end of this month.
But if you already know the stakes of this race and the importance of this deadline and are ready to contribute now, use this link:
**Here’s the link to donate:[https://act.electjon.com/go/Donate-Now-FEC](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-sep26.MEWcSy&refcode=em260912-1-subs&utm_campaign=em260912-1-subs&t=2&akid=2857%2E5691347%2EcDWTb3)**
Otherwise, please give us a minute to explain:
This is the last FEC end-of-quarter deadline of the race, and it's a big one. When it ends, we're _legally required_ to report not just what we've raised, but the number of donations we've received will be public as well.
Everyone will be watching: Not just Mike Collins, but the entire Republican Party (and their Super PACs...), Donald Trump and MAGA, the press, and more.
They’re looking for any signs of weakness in our campaign. If they think we look vulnerable, they’ll pour even more into Georgia to buy this race.
We can’t afford to let that happen.
[**So please, chip in today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-sep26.MEWcSy&refcode=em260912-1-subs&utm_campaign=em260912-1-subs&t=3&akid=2857%2E5691347%2EcDWTb3)
$5 because Jon is the only Democratic Senator running for reelection in a state Trump won.
$5 because Republican Super PACs and dark money groups have _already spent_ more than $30 million and _will spend_ whatever it takes to win this race.
$5 because our campaign is funded primarily by lots of donations given by people giving what they can, when they can.
We know that $5 may not seem like it can take on Donald Trump, mega-donors like Elon Musk, and the entire Republican Party. But when lots and lots of people are chipping in, it will add up fast. So please:
[**Rush a $5 contribution directly to Jon Ossoff’s campaign. body:
Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton

| | | |
#
---
---
|
---
Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. **They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing.** You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. **This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it.** Sadly, that's not going to happen. You may hear party leaders say they "hope" Ken Paxton wins and they "hope" President Trump helps him, but they have closed their wallets and are quietly rooting for him to lose. They don't want another conservative in the Senate who will hold them accountable, and they would love to tell everyone that Ken Paxton was a bad candidate who cost them the majority, even though they're the ones who kneecapped and left him for dead. **TAKE ACTION** **Conservatives are right to be mad about this, but being mad won't change it. We need to take immediate action.** [**Please support Ken Paxton with a direct contribution today.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0MFuwyAQBNCvwbdYsAY7PnCoVPmWXnu0tsuS0GKwgKRpv75K-we9j2ae5vW0njDEkM4vuLEtza-lrpUTNj7nPeUtJ_7yuTS-Y11BwniQ80HBitTCjVeNnbOOHCrq2KrpOAMYGFR3sQBkvPZgjHKTVnTUcsJhmhXJUYGBLthHn5wVKCMljL0hM0rtNSutvPaD0BIjl9YX3q9vMRCmhvXD50LcU966aC-t7VUMTwIWAUtluhbu__yUU-Vyw4ezPuIClvsImxKwODEsJIbn9O6O32OBILti3f4ZYgx1nISW5w1D_B1p_7vlZuEnAAD__xdpcg0) SCF will pay all processing fees and transfer 100% of your contribution directly to his campaign. Nothing will do more to defeat the feckless GOP establishment than electing true conservative fighters to the U.S. Senate. This is how we must respond. We must win even with the odds stacked against us. We do it because it's our legacy. We love this country and don't give up; we don't back down. Thank you for considering this request and for doing so much to help fight for America's future.

Invest in Democrats that will fight tooth and nail to defend Social Security >>

| **↓We wanted to make sure you were aware of this↓** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139061920/646107445/-1005693264?amount=10&amounts=5,10,25,50,100,250,500&refcode=NDCAF_20260912_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84Mjc1NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMTFhNGRhOC1iYWFlLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=xIpfHHunqyKQe9g6_R-SCmyDhzWoNyyFci20_nKL1wY=) MAGA Republicans are fully committed to depriving hard-working Americans of the benefits they have earned.

**Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans are dismantling Social Security through backdoor cuts.**

name: Citizens for Amanda Pusczek
subject: On the Trail This Weekend: Meet Amanda Across AL-04 (Sept 12–13)
body:
Join Amanda in Cullman, Jasper, and Fayette for town halls, festivals, and pop-up meetups.
---
| | | | | |
---
| | | Hi Team,
Grassroots momentum in Alabama’s 4th District happens on the ground—listening to neighbors, showing up in our communities, and having direct conversations about the future of our district.
Amanda is hitting the road across Cullman, Walker, and Fayette counties this weekend, and we’d love to see you out on the trail. Bring a friend, wear your walking shoes, and join us at any of the stops below:
**Saturday, September 12**
* **1:00 PM | Cullman Democratic HQ Open House** 105 2nd Ave SE, Cullman, AL _Kick off the afternoon with fellow supporters._
* **2:30 PM | Pop-Up Meet & Greet**103 1st Ave NE, Cullman, AL _Casual conversation and direct Q &A in downtown Cullman._
* **5:30 PM | Outdoor Town Hall Outside Rep. Robert Aderholt’s Office** 205 4th Ave NE, Cullman, AL _A public town hall focused on holding leadership accountable and outlining real solutions for AL-04 families._
* **7:30 PM | Foothills Festival** Downtown Jasper, AL _Connecting with community members, enjoying local music, and talking about local issues._

**Sunday, September 13**
* **4:30 PM | Pop-Up Meet & Greet**110 21st St NE, Fayette, AL _An afternoon gathering to discuss rural infrastructure, healthcare access, and community priorities._

Every conversation we have moves this district forward. If you plan to attend or want to help canvass at any of these events, let us know by let us know by replying to this email or checking in with our field team when you arrive.
See you out there,**Team Amanda Pusczek**

_Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. _ A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance.

They told her something every child deserves to hear: **You are loved. **They promised to protect her and help her get an education. And Nadia willingly went with them. She left behind a horrible life and came home to parents who would raise her as their own. Peter, Nadia's story is one reason **Sound of Freedom Foundation** works with groups like House Parent Project.My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie _Sound of Freedom_ because after learning what traffickers do to innocent children, I could not simply look away.For me, it stopped being a movie. It became a calling. Today, the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** carries that mission forward. Our mission is simple: **Stop the sale of God 's children.** House Parent Project shares that commitment. Their house parents give these children the love and care they've never known.

And Nadia shows what can happen when a child is not abandoned. A couple of years after her rescue, the team found Nadia's sister, Sofia. She was suffering through many of the same horrors. They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. **Their hearts were still with the children. **Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, **they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes**. The child who once needed someone to find her**grew up to help care for children who need to be found. **That is**restoration**. That is **hope**. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects **between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day**.

When it is safe, they work to restore children to healthy homes with family members. When that cannot happen, the homes may raise these children as their own until they grow up, get jobs, and go to college. More than **40 children that were residents stayed to become staff after they grew up**. Others have grown up and married national pastors and missionaries. But there's a problem. **The phone never stops ringing.**

clean_body: A frightened 15-year-old was given a chance. See where she is today. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Peter, Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance. They told her something every child deserves to hear: You are loved. They promised to protect her and help her get an education. And Nadia willingly went with them. She left behind a horrible life and came home to parents who would raise her as their own. Peter, Nadia's story is one reason Sound of Freedom Foundation works with groups like House Parent Project.My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie Sound of Freedom because after learning what traffickers do to innocent children, I could not simply look away.For me, it stopped being a movie. It became a calling. Today, the Sound of Freedom Foundation carries that mission forward. Our mission is simple: Stop the sale of God 's children. House Parent Project shares that commitment. Their house parents give these children the love and care they've never known. And Nadia shows what can happen when a child is not abandoned. A couple of years after her rescue, the team found Nadia's sister, Sofia. She was suffering through many of the same horrors. They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. Their hearts were still with the children. Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes. The child who once needed someone to find hergrew up to help care for children who need to be found. That isrestoration. That is hope. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day. When it is safe, they work to restore children to healthy homes with family members. When that cannot happen, the homes may raise these children as their own until they grow up, get jobs, and go to college. More than 40 children that were residents stayed to become staff after they grew up. Others have grown up and married national pastors and missionaries. But there's a problem. The phone never stops ringing. There is always another child. Another crisis and another need. And the resources are slim. Providing three meals for one child costs about $4 a day. And that doesn't include clothes, shoes, diapers, or all the other things children need. Jesus said: " Let the little children come to me." (Matthew 19:14) I believe we have a duty to hear the cries of children who cannot protect themselves. Because when good people stay quiet, evil has room to grow. But when good people stand together,lives can change. Nadia is living proof. Peter, will you help us stand with House Parent Project and the house parents caring for children like Nadia today? "=" $25 can help feed a child fornearly a week $50 can help feed a child fornearly two weeks $100 can help feed a childfor25 days $200 can help**feedtwo children for 25 days That 's three meals every day. Maybe we cannot answer every call today. But together, we can help answer the next one. Please give now. And please pray for the children and for those caring for them. Share this mission with someone you love. Because this truth must be heard around the world: God 's children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. It costs about $4 to provide one child with three meals for one day**. I've been asked a lot lately how I feel about this race in light of recent polls. My answer often starts with reminding people about 2016.
That year, I ran for Governor for the first time. I was fighting to unseat Republican Governor Pat McCrory, and nobody had defeated an incumbent Governor in North Carolina for more than 150 years. Despite these odds, I knew we had the team behind us to win and make history.
The polls showed us with a consistent lead hovering around 54% as we got closer to Election Day. We worked hard and took nothing for granted, yet many people let up a bit thinking we had the race in the bag. It was hard to understand what any of it meant for the race.
Then came Election Night and the race was too close to call. We ended that night with about a 5,000-vote lead out of about 4.6 million votes cast.
After a long recount and unfounded claims about voter fraud raised by the incumbent Republican Governor, the results finally came in: **We had won the race by 10,277 votes, just .22% of the total.**
Now, take a second to think about that. Despite months of favorable numbers, despite the winds seeming to blow in our direction, that race could have just as easily gone the other way. A razor-thin margin like that doesn't leave much room to rest, no matter how good the polling looked along the way.
I'm glad we won even though I know some of our supporters look their foot off the gas. I learned a lot from that race and I think about it frequently when I look at the numbers coming in today.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/7310f42d-12db-44a9-bd60-babc0c7d677b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **So where do things stand now?**
I know it can be confusing and overwhelming when different polls seem to tell slightly different stories. I want to walk you through how I'm reading these numbers, why they matter and where things currently stand.
In early September of 2016, right around this same time in this election calendar, I was up around 51% in the polls. Right now, in this Senate race, I'm up right around 50%.
So we've been here before.
We know what tends to happen next. That's why we can't slow down and will continue fighting hard every day to flip this crucial Senate seat.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/7310f42d-12db-44a9-bd60-babc0c7d677b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **What history tells us**
The history of U.S. Senate races in our state shows us that the polls will keep tightening as Election Day gets closer. We also know that there will likely be polls that show us the occasional spike that suggests a bigger lead than is really there. It's tempting, in moments like that, to relax a little and assume everything's going to be just fine.
But 2016 taught me -- and all of us -- not to make that assumption. Polls are a snapshot in time, not a prediction of the election outcome. They are helpful to show us trends, along with people's opinions about our agenda. But a lead can easily evolve into an election night loss, especially when the campaign ends up being outspent. And it's not just my own experience guiding this caution. Take a look at what happened just last month in Wisconsin Florida and Michigan, where poll after poll showed big leads that led to losses. Those races are recent, real reminders that polling has limits and that a lead today does not necessarily predict the results of Election Day.
So while polls are useful, and give us a real sense of how North Carolinians are feeling and where the race currently stands, I don't let them affect how hard I work.
Because at the end of the day, polls may tell us what is right or wrong, but they don't win elections. The hard work we do on the ground -- the doors we knock, the phone calls we make and the conversations we have with voters across this state are what really matter. That's what pushed me through the finish line in 2016, and that's how we'll win this time, too.
**So if you 're ready to help our team knock on more doors, run more ads and reach more voters so we can win this critical U.S. Senate race, [will you chip in $5 today?](https://substack.com/redirect/7310f42d-12db-44a9-bd60-babc0c7d677b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Let's flip North Carolina and take back the Senate.
Thank you,
Roy Cooper

Polls are a snapshot in time, not a prediction of the election outcome. They are helpful to show us trends, along with people's opinions about our agenda. But a lead can easily evolve into an election night loss, especially when the campaign ends up being outspent. And it's not just my own experience guiding this caution. Take a look at what happened just last month in Wisconsin Florida and Michigan, where poll after poll showed big leads that led to losses. Those races are recent, real reminders that polling has limits and that a lead today does not necessarily predict the results of Election Day. So while polls are useful, and give us a real sense of how North Carolinians are feeling and where the race currently stands, I don't let them affect how hard I work. Because at the end of the day, polls may tell us what is right or wrong, but they don't win elections. The hard work we do on the ground -- the doors we knock, the phone calls we make and the conversations we have with voters across this state are what really matter. That's what pushed me through the finish line in 2016, and that's how we'll win this time, too. So if you 're ready to help our team knock on more doors, run more ads and reach more voters so we can win this critical U.S. Senate race, Let's flip North Carolina and take back the Senate. Thank you, Roy Cooper | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

name: Ilhan Omar
subject: Block the Bombs.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Americans are tired of seeing our tax dollars being used to commit war crimes.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2465%2E791427%2E2ot4or)
Friend, I’m going to be straightforward here. I hope you’ll read on.
The US relationship with Israel has been front and center in elections across the country this year.
And what we’ve seen is candidates who call out the Gaza genocide and reject AIPAC winning from Pennsylvania, to Colorado, to Michigan, to right here in Minnesota. **This should surprise no one.**
For almost three years now, we have watched as the Israeli military has waged a brutal military campaign, killing tens of thousands of civilians, murdering innocent kids and babies, and displacing millions of people. War crimes have been committed on an almost daily basis, from the restriction of humanitarian aid to the intentional targeting of entire families. This, backdropped by almost 80 years of illegal occupation, ethnic cleansing, and apartheid.
And what has been the establishment's response to this historic injustice? To continue to stand by Israel’s actions. To continue to send Israel billions of dollars in military aid and weapons. And to tell people they had it all wrong — and even punish them — when they spoke up, protested, and pushed for change from a place of moral clarity.
It’s no wonder that that same establishment is now stunned that Americans are outraged, and losing ground fast.
**It’s been an uphill battle, but the movement for dignity, peace, and self-determination for Palestine is growing larger every day, and thanks to your tireless efforts, we are electing more pro-Palestine champions than at any time in American history.**
Americans are tired of seeing our tax dollars being used to commit war crimes. We are done with being told that we must support occupation and apartheid. And we are fed up with AIPAC and Israel’s allies in the US spending millions of dollars to defeat progressives and maintain the status quo.
[**Friend, I am a proud sponsor of the _Block the Bombs Act,_ which would restrict military aid to Israel. If you want to keep this movement pushing forward, add your name as a citizen co-sponsor of this legislation and help us keep turning up the pressure.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_block_the_bombs_cosponsor_sept26/?source=em260912-1-subs-90&refcode2=2465.791427.2ot4or&akid=2465%2E791427%2E2ot4or)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_block_the_bombs_cosponsor_sept26/?source=em260912-1-subs-90&refcode2=2465.791427.2ot4or&akid=2465%2E791427%2E2ot4or)**
Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. famously said, "The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice," and we are watching that happen in real time.
Palestinians have endured decades of injustice, but we are making progress towards an eventual peace for _everyone_ in the region. It starts with ending the US government’s unconditional support for Israel and redefining our approach around international law and universal human rights.
In solidarity,
Ilhan Omar
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_block_the_bombs_cosponsor_sept26/?source=em260912-1-subs-90&refcode2=2465.791427.2ot4or&akid=2465%2E791427%2E2ot4or)**

Ilhan is counting on our people-powered grassroots movement to fund this campaign. If you can, stand with us by **[making a contribution today](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/io-em-footer/?refcode=em-footer&t=5&refcode2=2465_791427_2ot4or&akid=2465%2E791427%2E2ot4or)**.

body:
While taking back the Senate majority is within our reach this November, we can’t take anything for granted.
#
Hi there,
With just over 7 weeks until Election Day, I want to give you an update on where things stand in Swing Left’s Must-Win races for the United States Senate. Overall, Democrats are in a strong position to flip the chamber this November.
**Polling numbers consistently show our target Democratic U.S. Senate candidates ahead of or neck-and-neck with their Republican opponents:**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-senate-2026.Ns7Ngr&refcode=em20260912-2752&t=1&akid=2752%2E1562180%2Ebuh9B3)

_All_ of these races will be close. While taking back the Senate majority is within our reach this November, we can’t take anything for granted. That’s why the Swing Left community is working to have hundreds of thousands of conversations with voters in swing districts and states that will decide these races, ahead of Election Day.
But it takes resources to do that work, which is why today, with just over 7 weeks to go, we’re asking you to [**make a donation of any amount to our Win The Senate Fund today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-senate-2026.Ns7Ngr&refcode=em20260912-2752&t=3&akid=2752%2E1562180%2Ebuh9B3)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-senate-2026.Ns7Ngr&refcode=em20260912-2752&t=4&akid=2752%2E1562180%2Ebuh9B3)**
Your donation will be split between each of the candidates listed above, with a portion also going to Swing Left to support our efforts to have Ground Truth conversations in competitive states across the country.
Thank you, as always, for being a part of the effort to build durable governing power for Democrats this year and beyond. We’ll keep you updated as things change!
Craig Auster
Political Director, Swing Left

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. name: Roy Cooper
subject: We’re in the final leg of the race.
body:
Together, we’ve built a grassroots movement unlike anything ever seen in North Carolina.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1309&source=&t=1&akid=3398%2E124072%2EzV5Zgj) | | | |
---
Peter,
It’s one thing to win a gubernatorial election. With outside spending pouring in, winning a U.S. Senate race is going to be another thing entirely – especially when you’re in a state that elected President Trump three times straight and hasn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate since 2008.
**However, this isn’t just North Carolina’s fight. This seat will decide Senate control until 2029.**
[**_With less than eight weeks left until Election Day and absentee ballots already being cast, can you pitch in $5 now to help me flip the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1309&amount=5&t=8&akid=3398%2E124072%2EzV5Zgj)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1309&amount=5&t=9&akid=3398%2E124072%2EzV5Zgj)
---
We’ve built a grassroots movement unlike anything ever seen in North Carolina. The New York Times is saying that our race is the best shot Democrats have to flip a red Senate seat this cycle.
And since President Trump anointed Michael Whatley of all people – a Big Oil lobbyist and MAGA loyalist – to be the GOP nominee, **it’s no wonder national Republicans are terrified.**
That’s why Stephen Miller, JD Vance and President Trump have all gone out of their way to publicly attack me.
That’s why dark-money groups are flooding the state with nearly $100 million so far in ads slandering me.
That’s why the Senate GOP’s top super PAC is currently spending more in North Carolina than almost anywhere else in the country to defeat me.
Since recent polls show my slim lead has shrunk down to the margin of error, it’s working.
Now, I know I ask a lot of you in these emails, but we’re in the final, most difficult stretch of the race. **While they have the money, we have you** – and your grassroots support is the only way I stand a chance of fighting back against the kind of Big Money that’s coming our way.
[**_I have nowhere else to turn, Peter, so I hope you’ll chip in $5 or anything you can right now to help me prove that no amount of dark money can buy North Carolina’s seat._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1309&amount=5&t=10&akid=3398%2E124072%2EzV5Zgj)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1309&amount=5&t=11&akid=3398%2E124072%2EzV5Zgj)

Thanks for everything,

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.
