name: Chris Pappas
subject: What I learned running in a race like this
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Nothing is guaranteed in a race this close.

I should know — I’ve won four times in a district called one of the
“swingiest” in the country. But now political experts across the country
agree: New Hampshire’s Senate seat is in jeopardy:

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1003&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Bloomberg[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1004&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Democratic Senate Seate at risk in New Hamsphire as Sununu Gains

The GOP and its dark money allies have pledged to spend over $45 million
in New Hampshire to boost John Sununu’s campaign, prop up Donald Trump’s
extreme agenda, and cement their majority in Washington.

To be direct, we cannot match them dollar-for-dollar.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1005&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]I
need you to step up right now if this campaign has any shot of regaining
the lead and beating Republicans this November. Will you pitch in
$5 or whatever you can today to keep New Hampshire blue and
flip the Senate?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&amount=5&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1024&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Donate $5 »

While my opponent has Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and a political dynasty on
his side, I have something they don’t: you and this grassroots team.

I couldn’t be more grateful for your support. But I’m asking you to take
your support even further at this critical moment. Together, we’ll be able
to out-work them and show that New Hampshire cannot be bought.

We deserve a New Hampshire where public servants are trusted to go to
Washington and fight to make things affordable for working families — not
just be yes-men for Donald Trump.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1025&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]That’s why I’m asking for your support today. If you’re with me, we
need all the help we can get to stop this Senate seat from flipping red.
Will you make a contribution of $5 or any amount to our
campaign before it’s too late?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260912_1.6I9svM&amount=5&refcode=em20260912-1&t=1044&akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris Pappas

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=8876%2E582294%2EA74AqI

name: Eric Pratt
subject: My roots in Minnesota’s Second District
body:
True representation begins with listening. Share your priorities with me.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ASIamEVr3_4?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

_**Prior Lake has been my home since the mid-1970s.**_ My mother taught school in Shakopee for over 25 years, my father worked in real estate, and my wife Tina and I raised our two children right here in the Second District.**I learned early on that government decisions directly impact working families.** That’s what led me to earn my MBA in Finance, spend 30 years in business leading fraud prevention efforts at U.S. Bank and Target, and serve on the Prior Lake–Savage School Board—where we eliminated a $1 million deficit, built a surplus, reduced property tax rates, and doubled student enrollment.I believe true representation begins with listening. My playbook for Congress isn't written by D.C. political consultants; it's guided by the values I’ve carried my whole life and the thousands of conversations I’ve had across our five counties.
---

Hey folks,
This one scares the hell out of me.
AI researchers are sounding the alarm about where this technology is headed, while too many of our political leaders are either asleep at the wheel or treating it like another arms race with China. We need a real conversation about who gets to decide our future--and whether ordinary people get any say at all.
* [**00:01:35**] An AI researcher resigns from Anthropic and warns that the biggest AI companies are "gambling with our lives."
* [**00:04:34**] Why letting tech billionaires race ahead without meaningful regulation could devastate jobs, communities, water, and our economy.
* [**00:07:15**] The China arms-race argument falls apart--and why we should be talking about international guardrails instead.
* [**00:10:46**] The danger may not look like _The Terminator_. It could be a slower erosion of our jobs, relationships, communities, and humanity.
* [**00:13:03**] J.B. Pritzker sounds the alarm on AI safety--and shows what serious political leadership on this issue could look like.

I'm not anti-AI. I've built an AI company, I use these tools, and I know they can do incredible things. But when researchers building this technology are warning about catastrophic risks, we have to listen. And when communities are worried about jobs, data centers, electricity costs, water, and their own ability to shape what happens where they live, they deserve a voice. This conversation is only getting started, and I'm going to keep digging into it. If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.

Cost of Living Families and individuals are dealing with rising everyday expenses and are looking for practical ways to make life more affordable. Local Services Residents have questions and concerns about the quality, accessibility, and responsiveness of local services. Jobs and the Local Economy Economic opportunity, small businesses, and maintaining a strong local workforce remain important topics for many people we speak with. Community Growth As our communities change and grow, residents are discussing infrastructure, development, transportation, and the impact of growth on neighborhoods.

When I got off active duty and came back home to the great state of Georgia, I quickly realized that despite having thousands of service members in our communities, **_Georgia is not a veteran-friendly state,_** between state taxes on military retirement and a healthcare system that treats veterans like an afterthought.
---
| [ ](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/PLC08N8dpkOSBGlSC_8m9A~~/AAPPABA~/26ugM1VcebxgLAiw7OT63ufHYkHzLaSNNrfVv2Y7hk7fn8yvu9o1k5IRUmSaLvjuO4IOSyQiSPeuzGAznyTVY-P6wBb5kA9tS5O_xh6It001qAcuSIv5xRu01MlbaSJxbV9NygpDcq8weSBbVPiFu6Bh6_nt9SKbxFSwcYA-Dr5PQFi6c5ffzjsCqXb7hC2H3CMrhagDQLVIOnqi7_FORI6QSgUpVrq5N9WYrLCpxlyrcJYYm92lKz4yVfzvaoGirwLMOxmzTY4QzANatsgRrwsJKsprXwGahlPmw61THBQ2Z2_J1H_-PsXuEgyZyRLm)
---
My last assignment was in Israel. I went from leading troops in high-stakes environments to coming back home and experiencing the sudden crash that so many service members face when transitioning back to civilian life. I knew I needed help, so I called Fort Benning. They directed me to a local mental health facility. I pulled up to that clinic as General Shawn Harris. I walked to the counter, and the receptionist looked right at me and said: _"We don't take TRICARE anymore."_ I had served 40 years. I had the rank, and I had the phone numbers to call people high up in the chain of command to fix my situation. But what if I was an E-4? If a young Specialist walked into that clinic without a star on their shoulder or a direct line to a general, they would have been turned away with nowhere to go. Without help, they could have ended up dead. I walked back out, sat in my car, and thought: **_This is why I 'm getting into politics._** **My blood boils when politicians like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth treat our military like a political backdrop or talk about veterans' benefits as something to slash and privatize.** Pete Hegseth and the political class in Washington love to wrap themselves in the flag, but when our service members come home broken, struggling, or needing care, they look the other way. They treat the men and women who put their lives on the line like line items on a spreadsheet instead of human beings who earned their care. Our troops and veterans don't need political posturing or lectures on culture wars from political appointees--they need a healthcare system that actually answers the phone when they call for help. I fought for this country for four decades, and I'm not going to sit quietly while politicians neglect the men and women who served alongside me. My Message to the Republican Convention...

| | | | Peter, Last night I walked off the stage after my speech at the Republican Convention in Dallas. _The energy was electric!_ It was an honor to address grassroots Republicans from all over Texas and the country... President Trump and Republicans have achieved so much in the past two years. We can't stop now. We must keep making America stronger, more prosperous, more affordable, and safer for Americans. We must help President Trump put America First and prevent the America-Last Democrats from regaining power. With your continued support, I know we will do everything we can to stop the Democrats from flipping Texas and from taking control of the United States Senate. This race in Texas is crucial. Friend, I recently visited the construction site of a proposed data center in Effingham County, Georgia. **Simply put, I’m alarmed.**
This would become one of the largest data centers in the country – right down the street from an elementary school. But the people who live in Effingham County haven’t had any say in the matter. The entire process has been cloaked in secrecy.
We’re seeing this happen all across Georgia and all across the country. Corporations come in and build these massive data centers with no input from the people who live in these communities. And in many cases, it’s driving up the cost of electricity, raising the price of water, and creating pollution.
**It has to stop. That’s why I’m calling for a moratorium on the construction of data centers.** This moratorium should only be lifted if corporations can ensure transparency and that the data centers won’t cause any spike in utility bills or pollution.

subject: Can you imagine being trafficked by your own stepfather?
body:
A little girl's stepfather trafficked her for 5 years. Then she found a way to ask for help.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6254351/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvVkV0WnJIZjJyRQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTI/LbmNsYmdCU2xxeA/qP2hpZHM9bmM0WkxTUkcwdVlXOGFscw/gaqV-aQ/s2qbd1a0570)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-aQ/sdkbaf4dd76)
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
Imagine you're eight years old, and you just lost your mom. You were taken across the border by the very man who was supposed to keep you safe. You're taken away from everyone who loves you.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-aQ/sdkbaf4dd76)
---
That was Jeanie. **For five years, her own stepfather trafficked her.** This makes me sick, and I imagine it does the same for you. Her sister never stopped searching. The FBI had a case open. But once Jeanie was taken to Mexico, she seemed impossible to find. **Then one night, Jeanie found her moment.** She quietly used her stepfather's phone and typed the words: **"Help me,"** her location, and a warning to her sister not to respond so her stepfather wouldn't see the message. **Friend, can you imagine the courage that took?**
---
When a **Sound of Freedom Foundation** partner was notified about the message, they had one small window before she'd be gone again. The team drove through the night, thirteen hours into cartel-controlled territory. At daybreak, they found her and got her out safely. Her first request once she was safe? **Pizza.** She hadn't had it in years. **Today, Jeanie is safe, healing, and thriving in a loving adoptive family.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-aQ/sdkbaf4dd76)
---
My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I produced the film **Sound of Freedom** , and for me, I thought it would be the finish line. It wasn't. The film was only the beginning. I heard stories like Jeanie's, and I could not walk away. This is why the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists. **Because the stories didn't stop when the credits rolled.** The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** has one mission: **To stop the sale of God's children.** We carry out that mission through five pillars:
---
* Prevention
* Intervention
* Education
* Information
* Influence

---
We fund the investigators who find trafficked children, the hotlines that answer the call, and the safe homes waiting when a child is finally rescued. **All of it happens because people like you refuse to look away.**
---

| | | | Peter, The Interior and Commerce Departments have officially pulled off a massive legal heist. They didn't pass a new law. They didn't issue a sweeping decree. Instead, they completely gutted the Endangered Species Act (ESA) by redefining a single word: **"harm."** [**Before you read on, will you help us fight back against this insanity by rushing an emergency donation to Public Land Warriors today?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/G9z3y-VPjWf8igxvJfjnMA~~/AAUS1hA~/tcYcnZTGdRUlyF2d_9Gv3anWPO8klaGcqLE0IkDKZNnbLDFUXA70RIiv0RIIrx-Wv0zWP5w7uVJv72lv2SpIUnCzEqQQj_gytNhCu-vv27ac1OM_WHnwGf2-NoiVrgKmVFhn4z97Q6fqSIyueX-lNmtGh_AR3kueWuLW1CY7eI9p3cjFAl9BlDqEe3gKCwEb87UU0pOH-VaKqJQ7kMtFH1jChe50qnmObazgVGGOQ_dpM-YYbvZEFa-0MBPf2ctk) **[**RUSH A DONATION »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/G9z3y-VPjWf8igxvJfjnMA~~/AAUS1hA~/tcYcnZTGdRUlyF2d_9Gv3anWPO8klaGcqLE0IkDKZNnbLDFUXA70RIiv0RIIrx-Wv0zWP5w7uVJv72lv2SpIUnCzEqQQj_gytNhCu-vv27ac1OM_WHnwGf2-NoiVrgKmVFhn4z97Q6fqSIyueX-lNmtGh_AR3kueWuLW1CY7eI9p3cjFAl9BlDqEe3gKCwEb87UU0pOH-VaKqJQ7kMtFH1jChe50qnmObazgVGGOQ_dpM-YYbvZEFa-0MBPf2ctk) ** For over 50 years—and backed by a landmark 1995 Supreme Court ruling—the federal government defined "harm" to include the significant degradation or destruction of an endangered animal's habitat. If you bulldozed a creature's nesting ground or poisoned its water supply so it couldn't eat, breed, or shelter, you were breaking the law. Under the administration’s new final rule, that protection is completely erased. As of right now, destroying an endangered species’ nest, breeding ground, or ancient forest habitat is entirely legal—as long as a corporation doesn't directly kill or injure the animal on camera at that exact second. It is a masterclass in bureaucratic cynicism, and the consequences are immediate:
* **The Winter Loopholes:** A property owner can now pave over the exact beaches migratory piping plovers rely on for spring nesting, because the birds happen to be south for the winter. When the birds return, their habitat is gone, but because no bird was crushed by a bulldozer in December, it’s completely legal.
* **The Clear-Cut Pass:** A timber conglomerate can clear-cut the mature pine trees that red-cockaded woodpeckers require to survive. The birds won't survive without them, but since the trees were cut down while empty, the extraction lobby gets a free pass.
* **The Corporate Playbook:** Interior Secretary Doug Burgum labeled 50 years of science-based habitat protections a "regulatory trap" that "burdened business." This rewrite is the ultimate payout to the mining, drilling, and real estate lobbies who want to strip-mine public assets without the "burden" of leaving a functional ecosystem behind.

They knew exactly how toxic this rule change was. During the comment period, the administration received over 220,000 public comments. An overwhelming **99% of Americans opposed the change** —including state wildlife agencies in deep-red states like Georgia and North Dakota, who warned the move would have "dire consequences." They ignored the public, they ignored the scientists, and they ignored their own state agencies to deliver a win for their corporate donors. We are funding targeted digital ad blitzes in the home districts of the politicians who rubber-stamped this gutting of the ESA. We are going to ensure that trading away America's wildlife heritage for corporate profit is the most expensive mistake they ever make. [**Will you chip in $25, $50, or $100 today to fund the rapid-response war chest and help us fight back against this absolute betrayal?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/G9z3y-VPjWf8igxvJfjnMA~~/AAUS1hA~/tcYcnZTGdRUlyF2d_9Gv3anWPO8klaGcqLE0IkDKZNnbLDFUXA70RIiv0RIIrx-Wv0zWP5w7uVJv72lv2SpIUnCzEqQQj_gytNhCu-vv27ac1OM_WHnwGf2-NoiVrgKmVFhn4z97Q6fqSIyueX-lNmtGh_AR3kueWuLW1CY7eI9p3cjFAl9BlDqEe3gKCwEb87UU0pOH-VaKqJQ7kMtFH1jChe50qnmObazgVGGOQ_dpM-YYbvZEFa-0MBPf2ctk) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/G9z3y-VPjWf8igxvJfjnMA~~/AAUS1hA~/tcYcnZTGdRUlyF2d_9Gv3anWPO8klaGcqLE0IkDKZNnbLDFUXA70RIiv0RIIrx-Wv0zWP5w7uVJv72lv2SpIUnCzEqQQj_gytNhCu-vv27ac1OM_WHnwGf2-NoiVrgKmVFhn4z97Q6fqSIyueX-lNmtGh_AR3kueWuLW1CY7eI9p3cjFAl9BlDqEe3gKCwEb87UU0pOH-VaKqJQ7kMtFH1jChe50qnmObazgVGGOQ_dpM-YYbvZEFa-0MBPf2ctk) ** They think they can solve their donors' problems by changing a definition in a dictionary. subject: I have never seen anything like this

body:
We have a slate of red-to-blue races to win — and we need your support to break the GOP’s grip on power.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260912-1&t=1&akid=4005%2E587540%2E31DXbX)
Peter,
Just about a week ago, I was in Bucks County, Pennsylvania knocking doors with our candidate, **Tim Hayes** , who’s in a must-win seat.
Tim had a list of 53 Republican voters’ doors for us to knock together, and I was shocked by how it went. Not one of the people whose doors we knocked on shut the door in our face (which is a rare experience when canvassing in even the most liberal of neighborhoods!). In fact, nearly all of the historically Republican voters we talked to expressed how disappointed they were with Trump. One of them even said they’re so fed up with the way things are, they’re voting straight Democrat on Election Day.
That experience in Bucks County gave me the energy, hope, and perspective to take on this final sprint to Election Day.
That’s why I couldn’t be more excited to announce that with our full candidate slate locked in for the midterms, we’re entering the final, decisive phase of our mission this cycle: **flipping red seats blue and breaking the GOP’s grip on power.**
To make sure we can go all in for our candidates, **[we’re launching a Red-to-Blue Fund](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260912_launch.RfrrsN&refcode=em20260912-4005&amount=5&t=2&akid=4005%2E587540%2E31DXbX)** that will ensure our candidates have the resources they need to compete against the GOP and win.
These seats are absolutely flippable with the right resources behind them:
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260912_launch.RfrrsN&refcode=em20260912-4005&t=3&akid=4005%2E587540%2E31DXbX)
These are the races that will break GOP supermajorities, flip state legislatures, and decide control of the House and Senate.
_This is a must-win election year._ And the truth is, our best shot at flipping these seats isn’t by playing it safe. Protecting the status quo is exactly what fed the disillusionment that has driven an entire generation of young voters to despair.
**Our work is the solution to that disillusionment.** We have to go all in on bold leaders who will actually center working-class priorities and offer a vision for the future that sparks hope, not apathy or fear.
In the coming weeks, I’ll be reaching out to tell you more about each and every one of these candidates so you know exactly who and what your support is powering. I want you to have a piece of these wins when we take them home in November.
**[So Peter, I’m asking you to make a $5 contribution to help us get our Red-to-Blue Fund off the ground. Winning in these competitive races is only possible with your support — I’d be grateful for whatever you can give today.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260912_launch.RfrrsN&refcode=em20260912-4005&amount=5&t=4&akid=4005%2E587540%2E31DXbX)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Hi friend,

Taking a quick break on the trail today to say a genuine thank-you.

Reading through your notes and seeing how many of you took the time to sign my 38th birthday card was incredible. These eight years in public office — since being elected shortly after my 30th birthday — have proved that community is everything. Seeing supporters across Maryland stand with us reminds me why we do this work every day.

Turning 38 is a great reminder of how far we have come, but also how critical the work ahead is.

We are in the final stretch, and building a House Democratic majority that holds this administration accountable depends on the energy we bring right now.

If you are ready to take that birthday momentum and channel it into winning this seat and taking back the House, pitching in a few bucks today goes a long way toward keeping our organizers on the ground and our message on the air.

Friend, As housing costs rapidly outpace wages, homelessness is on the rise. Trump is also gutting enforcement of our housing rights and threatening to lock up our unhoused neighbors. We must speak up! **Having access to a safe place to live is a human right, and we have the resources to permanently house all Americans in need** — including about 1 million K-12 students who experience homelessness each year. When the Senate comes back next week, they’ll consider the annual military budget bill. The House-passed version would spend **nearly $1 trillion of our taxpayer dollars on war and weapons corporations**. The nonprofit group Public Citizen says that **just one year of this budget would “house every homeless person in the U.S.****_for_********_121 years_****.”** **[Could you sign on to demand Congress eradicate homelessness in the richest country in the history of the world?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTAaMWCo82TreuofHNKXZ1vsI-8uoczhvCcMB4ZzbYT9Fb3p_I3N4IHUyF51fdCs0NeNjX-INpkw37VkRQc1l4EOuJCp7fHkCjB4p0zBsPEIvgyg1_xG_lxVB1p7rrGT7JEb4q2DoWVe_jEq_dr0YKq0BHfhC2U44JAX04kHoLTyOzvZiEGrO24z82dfYb8KrDU06X_QI94MWzyWyNnRrs0rKD8EjN0EICrYgEqcGRrgRiUO-l1OUl0zfI3ysQfdrSN-JcgetFoZj_BiQ9PqW96J6DLuRVZpJB1y5Rjq2saBMJF7yTmIOp43nVRyJMaMBRQ/4tz/j-oN0wrlSQKW3JIKsrhmQA/h1/h001.qBhphnnFdipsqQ88cQqrLjt4ZwUxwai1D5Ui5kOOIwo)** | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTAaMWCo82TreuofHNKXZ1vsI-8uoczhvCcMB4ZzbYT9Fb3p_I3N4IHUyF51fdCs0NfCLooTabk0HoD0GCnAuQTY4TMoTi3POrbfyd-29JuEYuGl8e3KXzWvPqv4c5tiAXlEHhNyBbMyWF96mvJ8YXDzdiz8W2zmLyMve4mpZHBSW1f1y5J3Z1EiFUSsPWrXVnF_KLCuhvSDdDOYUZt6iMNIM15TRBNi7zgyyYegqlDuolqMADl7XCsQiFCi2NvRcV9H9B5CsKTykxcmlihj7opFrr5SaYabeh2WLSFqsbHMN7-8NOIuaGA7_mAhF_RwsBQ/4tz/j-oN0wrlSQKW3JIKsrhmQA/h2/h001.U_yybOrxud7Lc9OUQ7JnO9W0FuHf9dk51p5PD-qskuw)

I’ve passed bills into law that**increase the supply of affordable housing, expand home ownership opportunities** to lower-wealth people, and **help families avoid eviction** by paying their utility bills.
But there’s so much more to do. I’m pushing to **expand banking opportunities and access to credit** , stop appraisal bias that devalues Black-owned homes, and **end discriminatory lending** and property tax practices that keep widening the wealth gap between Black and white families.
And right now, **people in my district need support with home repairs after last week’s storms**. So far, I’ve brought more than $7 million to my district to help seniors and flood victims repair and stay in their homes. I also passed a bill securing $3 billion for home repairs and neighborhood revitalization across the country, but we need to get this funding signed into law.
Here are some urgently-needed policies I’ve introduced, which Congress should pass as soon as possible:
* The **_Youth Homelessness Guaranteed Income Pilot Program Act_**. Young people experiencing homelessness crafted this bill to provide monthly direct cash assistance to young people in need.
* The **_Unhoused Persons Bill of Rights_** , which declares our neighbors’ human rights and provides solutions for the federal government to permanently end the unhoused crisis.
* The **_Tenant Empowerment Act_** , which would strengthen HUD tenant protections and provide renters in public housing with the tools necessary to improve the quality of their homes.
* Last week I also co-sponsored the******_No Homeless Detention Centers Act_** , which would prevent Trump’s threats by banning federal dollars from forcing unhoused people into detention-like facilities, and banning forced labor at such facilities.

Every day, I’m fighting back against Trump’s attacks on our housing rights, including his attempts to dismantle our fair housing laws and gut the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
Last year I requested $600 million to fund the State Veterans Homes program, which provides housing and supportive care through the Department of Veterans Affairs. I promise to keep fighting for veterans’ and everyone’s right to housing.
In my district I’ve also:
* Held housing justice hearings
* Created a local housing justice legislative working group
* Brought more than $5.5 million federal dollars for affordable and supportive housing, which is helping our seasoned residents, new moms, and young people experiencing homelessness

Always serving you,
Rashida

| | | Let's talk about your grocery bill, because I don't think it's an accident that it keeps climbing. Every time you check out at the store, you're told the same story: supply chains, avian flu, inflation, forces beyond anyone's control. And sure, some of that is real. But here's what they don't tell you: While your bill keeps climbing, food company profits keep hitting record highs. Both things are true at the same time, and that is not a coincidence. I've spent years on this fight. As a subcommittee chairman, I investigated the biggest meat processing companies in the country demanding to know why beef, pork, and chicken prices kept rising for families even as their profits soared. Their own earnings told a different story than the excuses they were giving the public. Egg prices jumped 14 percent in just the first few weeks of Trump's second term — despite his explicit campaign promise to bring prices down "starting on day one." I wrote directly to the White House and said what needed to be said: this isn't a failed campaign promise. It's a crisis for every family whose dollars don't stretch as far as they used to. Here's what I've learned from doing this work: when a handful of massive corporations control most of what ends up on your plate, they don't need a conspiracy to raise prices together. They just need to know they can get away with it — and count on you having nowhere else to go. **There is no equal opportunity if the game is rigged — and few things are more rigged, or more personal, than being squeezed every single week just to feed your family.** This is exactly why Equal Opportunity Now exists. clean_body: | | | | = | | | Let's talk about your grocery bill, because I don't think it's an accident that it keeps climbing. Every time you check out at the store, you're told the same story: supply chains, avian flu, inflation, forces beyond anyone's control. And sure, some of that is real. But here's what they don't tell you: While your bill keeps climbing, food company profits keep hitting record highs. Both things are true at the same time, and that is not a coincidence. I've spent years on this fight. As a subcommittee chairman, I investigated the biggest meat processing companies in the country demanding to know why beef, pork, and chicken prices kept rising for families even as their profits soared. Their own earnings told a different story than the excuses they were giving the public. Egg prices jumped 14 percent in just the first few weeks of Trump's second term — despite his explicit campaign promise to bring prices down "starting on day one." I wrote directly to the White House and said what needed to be said: this isn't a failed campaign promise. It's a crisis for every family whose dollars don't stretch as far as they used to. Here's what I've learned from doing this work: when a handful of massive corporations control most of what ends up on your plate, they don't need a conspiracy to raise prices together. They just need to know they can get away with it — and count on you having nowhere else to go. There is no equal opportunity if the game is rigged — and few things are more rigged, or more personal, than being squeezed every single week just to feed your family. This is exactly why Equal Opportunity Now exists. We are fighting to elect leaders who will take on corporate price-gouging directly — leaders who understand that a grocery bill shouldn't be a monthly test of how much a family can absorb before something breaks. = = | | | Your grocery bill shouldn't be a corporate profit strategy. body:
| | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: | | | | = | | Peter, Cait Conley here. I am the Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District and will officially face off against Mike Lawler this November. This is one of only three districts nationwide that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican. There is no path for Democrats to take back the House without winning this seat. = | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | I’m running for Congress not because this was ever part of some big life plan. But because the country I was willing to die for, the one I’ve lost countless friends defending, is becoming something I barely recognize. We cannot let this happen. Not on our watch. My opponent, Republican Mike Lawler, has a massive fundraising advantage over us. That means that we are the underdogs heading into the general election. From here on out, we can expect the attacks and mudslinging to only increase. It’s going to be an uphill battle. But I’ve never shied away from a tough fight. In the special operations community, we have a saying: “Run to the sound of the guns.” That’s what I’ve done my entire life. I joined the Army after 9/11. I deployed six times overseas, serving in combat zones like Iraq and Afghanistan, hunting down brutal terrorists to keep America and the world safe. Part of taking on tough fights means knowing when to ask for help. And today, I need to ask for your help. = | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | Let’s take back the House. clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Peter, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! For the truth, Nick Shirley P.S. -- A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. It’s imperative that we stop every effort to undermine the census and fair maps.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139071501/646143170/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQxMzBiMjZiLWNiYWUtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=sBz1rtj2H9W28qKo_YDbU6ypXi8-E3JOSrve3FcJI7U=&emci=fad5e6e7-42ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=d130b26b-cbae-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=8431045)

Peter, you and I know that this White House is a threat to democracy — we’ve watched them orchestrate a national redistricting crisis that has already ripped power away from voters in several states... _But President Trump and his MAGA allies don’t want to stop there_. One of the quieter parts of this power grab involves creating an uneven playing field in 2030 and beyond — that’s why they’re going after the U.S. Census. **Fair elections and fair representation depend on an accurate census.** The census provides a highly detailed picture of who is represented in a locality and how policies impact those communities. It’s a powerful tool to ensure representative democracy works. **But in its attempt to manipulate the 2030 Census, the White House is aiming to ignore race, gender, and sexual orientation — and stop counting undocumented immigrants.** Here’s the thing: The 14th Amendment is crystal clear about who the census must count — every person in a state, regardless of citizenship. **This scheme is as unconstitutional as it is an affront to our democracy. Ready to do something about it?[Make a gift to the NDRC to support the broader work to fight back and defend fair representation for all.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139071502/646143171/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_CensusAttack_email_20260912-NDRC-Tier1-CensusAttack_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260912-NDRC-Tier1-CensusAttack_&utm_campaign=CensusAttack&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQxMzBiMjZiLWNiYWUtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=sBz1rtj2H9W28qKo_YDbU6ypXi8-E3JOSrve3FcJI7U=)** The census is the people’s data. It was created for the people to ensure government represents the people — not the interests of politicians. (You can see why Donald Trump isn’t a fan of an accurate census count.) In addition to ensuring fair maps, the data collected guides allocations for state funding. Here’s the thing: The first Trump White House tried its best to distort the census last time around. And the fair maps movement took them to court — and ultimately we stopped this unconstitutional plan. But the court didn’t discard the Trump Administration’s scheme for legal reasons; it did so for procedural ones. A lot has changed in the last six years, and the courts have been a whole lot friendlier to Trump’s whims. We can’t just sit back and hope for the best. The NDRC’s Litigation and Policy team has been closely monitoring updates from the Census Bureau to ensure the fair maps movement can respond. We are dedicated to fighting back against any attempt by the White House or any of its allies to mess with the census, and you can help. [**Give today to strengthen our opposition to MAGA’s efforts to handpick the people who get to have a voice in this country. Democracy’s future depends on stopping this threat now.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139071503/646143172/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_CensusAttack_email_20260912-NDRC-Tier1-CensusAttack_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260912-NDRC-Tier1-CensusAttack_&utm_campaign=CensusAttack&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQxMzBiMjZiLWNiYWUtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=sBz1rtj2H9W28qKo_YDbU6ypXi8-E3JOSrve3FcJI7U=) Thank you for taking on this fight alongside us, Ted Corcoran

## The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you!
**[Become a paid subscriber today and access the Live Capitalist chat](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6372eb-03e8-48ae-a385-9af1cf10d1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe here now](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6372eb-03e8-48ae-a385-9af1cf10d1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
I hate islam.
Let me make it abundantly. I have too much respect for you, the reader, and too much respect for myself, to soften that unconventional opening thesis with the milquetoast, prerequisite qualifiers of cautious political correctness which pepper our postmodern society.
I hate islam. I will not buffer the sentiment with the effete qualifier "radical islam" or the false "islam has contributed to our culture" or the castrated "some of my best friends are muslim". I'm too tired and too angry to pull punches when we should be sharpening swords.
Metaphorically, of course.
Islam is not our friend. Michigan's democrat senatorial candidate the abundantly muslim Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed [told an audience](https://substack.com/redirect/52c90605-6de8-481f-b166-71a8ec58cc1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2018 "you may not hate muslims, but muslims hate you." Charming. May he know the feeling is mutual, though I won't "hate" people as my Lord commands me to love my enemy.
Curious, that our God calls on us to love whereas his god tells him to behead. See if you can detect the subtle difference.
I can love but still recognize my enemy, and I never pretend he is anything other. "The enemy of my enemy is my friend" is terrible strategy. The enemy of my enemy could very well be my enemy, and in that situation, let them destroy each other while you drink with friends.
Curious, Christ drank wine with his Disciples whereas the prophet of islam married and raped a 6-year-old girl. See if you can detect that subtle difference.
I find it unnerving to write this op-ed some 30,000 feet in the air on the 25th anniversary of 9/11. I'm not thrilled to be at the airport today of all days, but I must eat, so I must work. And I must not let them win. Islam would love to know that even one American today is afraid and curtailed his behavior fearing what new surprise they might have planned.
* * *
* * *
## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6372eb-03e8-48ae-a385-9af1cf10d1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
So, here I am, on a United flight while at this exact moment 25 years ago all aircraft had been grounded and American air space closed. Unnerving is an understatement.
I'm a New Yorker, and for us 9/11 hits hard. 25 years later, it still does.
And I mean real New Yorkers, not the interlopers who see New York City as a steppingstone for political ambition. At 30,000 feet on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 I put out a [rage tweet](https://substack.com/redirect/ec86baa0-dcdb-4112-a770-9b14dff46213?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about live footage of fake New Yorker Alexandria Ocasio Cortez and fake New Yorker, fake American, the muslim mayor of the city Zohan Bin-Whatever, having a good ole laugh as the names of 3000 victims were read aloud. Yup. They're caught on camera laughing, not even smart enough to sit in silence stone-faced for 90 minutes out of respect for the dead, grasping the gravity of the moment.
Selfish, vile children. One by religion, the other by choice.
A similar video crushed President Joe Biden. Joe looking at his watch during the arrival of fallen American servicemen, causalities from his disastrous Afghanistan withdrawal. He never recovered from that moment. Perhaps this video of AOC yucking it up at the 9/11 memorial could end her presidential campaign before it even launches.
I visited the 9/11 memorial only once. Those two, vast footprints of the former skyscrapers falling into nothingness, draining forever, a void never filling. I found no occasion to laugh.
Dad and I went to see it about 10 years ago. Dad knew, without exaggeration, two hundred people who were killed that day. Probably more as anyone would after several decades in the tight-knit Wall Street community. He wrote down the locations of a few names to find along the waterfall edge.
We found one at a corner. Mc something. I can't recall it. I looked at the [full list of names](https://substack.com/redirect/2a11dc36-e73e-4fe8-ba78-9af4cc7d92a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and there are 64 Mc's so I don't venture a guess. I watched dad silently run his fingers over the embossed name looking at the water fall and fall again into the abyss.
You can see what AOC found so funny.
Dad was not an emotional person. On 9/12 my sister saw him leave the room to go cry in private. I cannot imagine my father crying.
Mom and Dad went to dozens of 9/11 memorials. Every one he could, sometimes with several on the same day. Memorials, not funerals. There were no funerals as there were no bodies. Some were his work friends, the people he saw 10 hours a day, Monday through Friday, for decades. Some were neighbors. Sons and daughters of friends. Funerals were the chance to comfort the bereaved and offer prayers for the soul's repose, as our faith requires.
We go to funerals because we love life. They go to funerals because they love death. The subtle differences are growing less so.
* * *
* * *
## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6372eb-03e8-48ae-a385-9af1cf10d1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
It hits harder for New Yorkers, not just the day itself or the aftermath, but the persistence. Mom and I ran into a neighbor in 2014, and in the course of small-talk, mom asked "how's so-and-so doing?" I can still see the look of shock and disbelief. "He died on 9/11". Shit. How did we not know? Thirteen years later, and we still didn't know.
If you have that experience, you don't laugh. Not at the memorial. Not on the anniversary. Not ever. We do not need to be told "never forget". But there are some who have nothing, or no one, to even remember.
Fairfax County, Virginia, home to a large muslim immigrant community, **[issued guidance](https://substack.com/redirect/1b373d8c-cf41-4072-a704-cc89a4159579?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to its public schools how to teach 9/11, and of course it includes "don't associate the 9/11 attack with islam or muslims". Let us pretend it was... like an earthquake, but even natural disasters the left blames on "climate change" and they blame that on "big oil" and so someone is at fault. But not 9/11. No.
Canada's state-run media, Canadian Broadcast Company, **[issued guidance](https://substack.com/redirect/f5fbfa7d-2a76-4dd4-af35-6c037d8872d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** not to call 9/11 a terrorist attack. Perhaps it was postpartum psychosis. If only the hijackers had gotten the right medicine...
The New York Times has on its **[front page](https://substack.com/redirect/4e6961ea-1714-4612-905c-98c921f13140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , right as I type this, not just one but two stories about the threat of.... you guessed it... islamophobia. 9/11 is our fault. Why not? Climate change is.
Stupid New York Times. The great Norm Macdonald (may he rest in peace) **[tweeted](https://substack.com/redirect/f46dee9f-cadb-4451-b284-7689b9e6c5fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** satirically almost 10 years ago: _What terrifies me is if ISIS were to detonate a nuclear device and kill 50 million Americans. Imagine the backlash against peaceful Muslims?_ Yes, as the expression goes, the New York Times did the meme.
A muslim teacher in Texas **[opposed](https://substack.com/redirect/6387647b-8d29-405d-b0ab-db751b6c4a52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the new, state-mandated 9/11 curriculum which rightfully links the terrorist attack to islam. She argued her 4th grade class is too young for such issues. Age-appropriateness is suddenly a criteria for subject matter worthiness. I hope pride month and "no Thanksgiving on stolen land" fall under this new guidance. Texas families should not want a woman dressed as a 9th century Bedouin teaching their children.
New York's Governor Kathy Hochul wrote an insipid, saccharine, and sophomoric **[op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/1e2b61de-aa3d-407d-b659-87aa676d1e87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** today, just word vomit unworthy of ass wiping, in which she wishes "Never Forget" could magically transform into "service". Let me summarize it: "My policies turned New York into a filthy hellhole, so why don't you 9/11 sorry sacks at least pick up a broom?"
At no point in her babydoll musings does she say "terrorism" let alone islam or muslim. No, Kathy pretends 3000 Americans were murdered because of meanness, and the way to stop the caliphate is through soup kitchens... "You know what Abdul, maybe don't pull the rip cord on your suicide vest because New Yorkers are recycling". The dumb woman already surrendered: last week she dutifully **[covered her hair](https://substack.com/redirect/c09de69d-f408-4439-b817-94733fafefbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to enter a mosque, because one most certainly does NOT want to insult men who perform clitorectomies on their own daughters. Stupid, naive Kathy swallowing the islamic scimitar.
How the world change in 25 years.
America certainly did, and by no means for the better. It is easy to go back hypothetically and say what we would have done had we been in charge, a linguistic construct of subjunctive mood and past perfect tense as complicated as it is futile but I'm done litigating the myriad bad decisions made by our elected officials. Now we must decide how to go forward, to protect and preserve, to prevent and prevail.
Such a decision demands eyes wide open to a vicious fact: there is no place on earth or in history where islam "coexists". From its demon spawn to poisoning north Africa destroying Christian monasteries, into Europe, from Lepanto to Vienna, Covadonga to the Island of Malta, islam attacks to conquer until someone stops it. Charlemagne understood this. King Jan Sobieksi understood this. John Quincy Adams understood this so clearly he crushed the Barbary Pirates to the point that the United States Marine Corp still sings about it.
* * *
* * *
## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/7e6372eb-03e8-48ae-a385-9af1cf10d1e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
They came back. Evil always returns. And 200 years later we have Somali pirates, except this time the American President resettled them in America where they opened fraudulent, government funded daycares. I'd say we did not learn our lesson. "_From the Halls of Montezuma to Day Cares of Minnesota ..._"
Islam does not coexist, despite the gay "Coexist" bumper sticker. Ask the gays at the Pulse Nightclub about coexisting with islam. Ask women at German Christmas Markets. Soldiers in Fort Hood. Writers at Charlie Hebdo. Partiers at Bataclan. Travelers in Brussels. Swimmers at Bondi Beach.
Centuries of the scourge of islam and we still see the deadly desire to baptize it. Just six days after 9/11 [President Bush](https://substack.com/redirect/81034da6-03c2-46be-8d10-6178e790847c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) went to an islamic center to praise it as the religion of peace. Bush is a good man, a good Christian man, who wants to see good in all people. A noble gesture that got many killed, as weakness does.
Seriously, where on earth is islam "peace"? Even Pope Leo idiotically called it a religion of peace. I marvel how people so powerful are so stupid. Dangerously so.
I have no more patience for stupidity or weakness, nor will I look for the good in people. And for that, I do not apologize. When a wolf is attacking your children, you do not try to tame it. Do not ask me to find a moderate response to "You may not hate muslims, but muslims hate you." Today there are members of Congress who, because of "Free Palestine" sloganeering, celebrate the Islamic attack on October 7th where hundreds of Jewish people at a musical festival were murdered and raped.
No more nuance. "Islam gave us algebra". I am disinterested in solving for x when x is trying to slit my throat.
"You offer no solutions!" I get that a lot. This is not an operating manual. It is thought and opinion, but I hope if it does not encourage you, it will at least shield you. Let me be your shield. I'll get the hate mail. I'll get the attacks. Next time I am subpoenaed to testify before Congress this will used this to discredit me. HATE SPEECH! It's fine. I'll be the bad guy so long as I change opinions and stiffen spines. And that is what is needed.
The first step in defeating evil is identifying it. Not excusing it. Not trying to tame it. Not attempting to reconcile with it. Identify it so you can destroy it before it destroys you.
Our posture before islam can no longer be that of First Lady Michelle Obama when Boko Haram kidnapped hundreds of Christian girls in Africa. Standing there with that sour puss frowny face holding a piece of shit sign "bring back our girls" as if her husband did not control the world's most powerful military. Our posture before islam President Trump on Christmas Day blowing Boko Harma into tiny falafel pieces. The world will be at peace if Boko Haram, Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, the IRGC, ISIS, Al Qaeda, all of them once again faced Charles "the Hammer" Martel and not Charles III.
Buy a dog and get some bacon. And in the words of Todd Beamer uttered 25 years ago today "Let's roll". We may not get control of the plane back, but I'd rather die trying than live defeated by evil.
**Honor and courage.**
P.S. I do not capitalize the words "islam" and "muslim" unless they are the first word of sentence. Even I must obey that rule of English grammar. I do this deliberately to offend. Show it no respect, not even autographical.

Centuries of the scourge of islam and we still see the deadly desire to baptize it. | | | Sep 12 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you! I hate islam. Let me make it abundantly. I have too much respect for you, the reader, and too much respect for myself, to soften that unconventional opening thesis with the milquetoast, prerequisite qualifiers of cautious political correctness which pepper our postmodern society. I hate islam. I will not buffer the sentiment with the effete qualifier "radical islam" or the false "islam has contributed to our culture" or the castrated "some of my best friends are muslim". I'm too tired and too angry to pull punches when we should be sharpening swords. Metaphorically, of course. Islam is not our friend. Michigan's democrat senatorial candidate the abundantly muslim Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed in 2018 "you may not hate muslims, but muslims hate you." Charming. May he know the feeling is mutual, though I won't "hate" people as my Lord commands me to love my enemy. Curious, that our God calls on us to love whereas his god tells him to behead. See if you can detect the subtle difference. I can love but still recognize my enemy, and I never pretend he is anything other. "The enemy of my enemy is my friend" is terrible strategy. The enemy of my enemy could very well be my enemy, and in that situation, let them destroy each other while you drink with friends. Curious, Christ drank wine with his Disciples whereas the prophet of islam married and raped a 6-year-old girl. See if you can detect that subtle difference. I find it unnerving to write this op-ed some 30,000 feet in the air on the 25th anniversary of 9/11. I'm not thrilled to be at the airport today of all days, but I must eat, so I must work. And I must not let them win. Islam would love to know that even one American today is afraid and curtailed his behavior fearing what new surprise they might have planned. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! So, here I am, on a United flight while at this exact moment 25 years ago all aircraft had been grounded and American air space closed. Unnerving is an understatement. I'm a New Yorker, and for us 9/11 hits hard. 25 years later, it still does. And I mean real New Yorkers, not the interlopers who see New York City as a steppingstone for political ambition. At 30,000 feet on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 I put out a about live footage of fake New Yorker Alexandria Ocasio Cortez and fake New Yorker, fake American, the muslim mayor of the city Zohan Bin-Whatever, having a good ole laugh as the names of 3000 victims were read aloud. Yup. They're caught on camera laughing, not even smart enough to sit in silence stone-faced for 90 minutes out of respect for the dead, grasping the gravity of the moment. Selfish, vile children. One by religion, the other by choice. A similar video crushed President Joe Biden. Joe looking at his watch during the arrival of fallen American servicemen, causalities from his disastrous Afghanistan withdrawal. He never recovered from that moment. Perhaps this video of AOC yucking it up at the 9/11 memorial could end her presidential campaign before it even launches. I visited the 9/11 memorial only once. Those two, vast footprints of the former skyscrapers falling into nothingness, draining forever, a void never filling. I found no occasion to laugh. Dad and I went to see it about 10 years ago. Dad knew, without exaggeration, two hundred people who were killed that day. Probably more as anyone would after several decades in the tight-knit Wall Street community. He wrote down the locations of a few names to find along the waterfall edge. We found one at a corner. Mc something. I can't recall it. I looked at the and there are 64 Mc's so I don't venture a guess. I watched dad silently run his fingers over the embossed name looking at the water fall and fall again into the abyss. You can see what AOC found so funny. Dad was not an emotional person. On 9/12 my sister saw him leave the room to go cry in private. I cannot imagine my father crying. Mom and Dad went to dozens of 9/11 memorials. Every one he could, sometimes with several on the same day. Memorials, not funerals. There were no funerals as there were no bodies. Some were his work friends, the people he saw 10 hours a day, Monday through Friday, for decades. Some were neighbors. Sons and daughters of friends. Funerals were the chance to comfort the bereaved and offer prayers for the soul's repose, as our faith requires. We go to funerals because we love life. They go to funerals because they love death. The subtle differences are growing less so. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! It hits harder for New Yorkers, not just the day itself or the aftermath, but the persistence. Mom and I ran into a neighbor in 2014, and in the course of small-talk, mom asked "how's so-and-so doing?" I can still see the look of shock and disbelief. "He died on 9/11". Shit. How did we not know? Thirteen years later, and we still didn't know. If you have that experience, you don't laugh. Not at the memorial. Not on the anniversary. Not ever. We do not need to be told "never forget". But there are some who have nothing, or no one, to even remember. Fairfax County, Virginia, home to a large muslim immigrant community, to its public schools how to teach 9/11, and of course it includes "don't associate the 9/11 attack with islam or muslims". Let us pretend it was... like an earthquake, but even natural disasters the left blames on "climate change" and they blame that on "big oil" and so someone is at fault. But not 9/11. No. Canada's state-run media, Canadian Broadcast Company, not to call 9/11 a terrorist attack. Perhaps it was postpartum psychosis. If only the hijackers had gotten the right medicine... The New York Times has on its , right as I type this, not just one but two stories about the threat of.... you guessed it... islamophobia. 9/11 is our fault. Why not? Climate change is. Stupid New York Times. The great Norm Macdonald (may he rest in peace) satirically almost 10 years ago: What terrifies me is if ISIS were to detonate a nuclear device and kill 50 million Americans. Imagine the backlash against peaceful Muslims? Yes, as the expression goes, the New York Times did the meme. A muslim teacher in Texas the new, state-mandated 9/11 curriculum which rightfully links the terrorist attack to islam. She argued her 4th grade class is too young for such issues. Age-appropriateness is suddenly a criteria for subject matter worthiness. I hope pride month and "no Thanksgiving on stolen land" fall under this new guidance. Texas families should not want a woman dressed as a 9th century Bedouin teaching their children. New York's Governor Kathy Hochul wrote an insipid, saccharine, and sophomoric today, just word vomit unworthy of ass wiping, in which she wishes "Never Forget" could magically transform into "service". Let me summarize it: "My policies turned New York into a filthy hellhole, so why don't you 9/11 sorry sacks at least pick up a broom?" At no point in her babydoll musings does she say "terrorism" let alone islam or muslim. No, Kathy pretends 3000 Americans were murdered because of meanness, and the way to stop the caliphate is through soup kitchens... "You know what Abdul, maybe don't pull the rip cord on your suicide vest because New Yorkers are recycling". The dumb woman already surrendered: last week she dutifully to enter a mosque, because one most certainly does NOT want to insult men who perform clitorectomies on their own daughters. Stupid, naive Kathy swallowing the islamic scimitar. How the world change in 25 years. America certainly did, and by no means for the better. It is easy to go back hypothetically and say what we would have done had we been in charge, a linguistic construct of subjunctive mood and past perfect tense as complicated as it is futile but I'm done litigating the myriad bad decisions made by our elected officials. Now we must decide how to go forward, to protect and preserve, to prevent and prevail. Such a decision demands eyes wide open to a vicious fact: there is no place on earth or in history where islam "coexists". From its demon spawn to poisoning north Africa destroying Christian monasteries, into Europe, from Lepanto to Vienna, Covadonga to the Island of Malta, islam attacks to conquer until someone stops it. Charlemagne understood this. King Jan Sobieksi understood this. John Quincy Adams understood this so clearly he crushed the Barbary Pirates to the point that the United States Marine Corp still sings about it. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! They came back. Evil always returns. And 200 years later we have Somali pirates, except this time the American President resettled them in America where they opened fraudulent, government funded daycares. I'd say we did not learn our lesson. "From the Halls of Montezuma to Day Cares of Minnesota ..." Islam does not coexist, despite the gay "Coexist" bumper sticker. Ask the gays at the Pulse Nightclub about coexisting with islam. Ask women at German Christmas Markets. Soldiers in Fort Hood. Writers at Charlie Hebdo. Partiers at Bataclan. Travelers in Brussels. Swimmers at Bondi Beach. Centuries of the scourge of islam and we still see the deadly desire to baptize it. Just six days after 9/11 went to an islamic center to praise it as the religion of peace. Bush is a good man, a good Christian man, who wants to see good in all people. A noble gesture that got many killed, as weakness does. Seriously, where on earth is islam "peace"? Even Pope Leo idiotically called it a religion of peace. I marvel how people so powerful are so stupid. Dangerously so. I have no more patience for stupidity or weakness, nor will I look for the good in people. And for that, I do not apologize. When a wolf is attacking your children, you do not try to tame it. Do not ask me to find a moderate response to "You may not hate muslims, but muslims hate you." Today there are members of Congress who, because of "Free Palestine" sloganeering, celebrate the Islamic attack on October 7th where hundreds of Jewish people at a musical festival were murdered and raped. No more nuance. "Islam gave us algebra". I am disinterested in solving for x when x is trying to slit my throat. "You offer no solutions!" I get that a lot. This is not an operating manual. It is thought and opinion, but I hope if it does not encourage you, it will at least shield you. Let me be your shield. I'll get the hate mail. I'll get the attacks. Next time I am subpoenaed to testify before Congress this will used this to discredit me. HATE SPEECH! It's fine. I'll be the bad guy so long as I change opinions and stiffen spines. And that is what is needed. The first step in defeating evil is identifying it. Not excusing it. Not trying to tame it. Not attempting to reconcile with it. Identify it so you can destroy it before it destroys you. Our posture before islam can no longer be that of First Lady Michelle Obama when Boko Haram kidnapped hundreds of Christian girls in Africa. Standing there with that sour puss frowny face holding a piece of shit sign "bring back our girls" as if her husband did not control the world's most powerful military. Our posture before islam President Trump on Christmas Day blowing Boko Harma into tiny falafel pieces. The world will be at peace if Boko Haram, Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, the IRGC, ISIS, Al Qaeda, all of them once again faced Charles "the Hammer" Martel and not Charles III. Buy a dog and get some bacon. And in the words of Todd Beamer uttered 25 years ago today "Let's roll". We may not get control of the plane back, but I'd rather die trying than live defeated by evil. Honor and courage. P.S. I do not capitalize the words "islam" and "muslim" unless they are the first word of sentence. Even I must obey that rule of English grammar. I do this deliberately to offend. Show it no respect, not even autographical. Daniel Turner is the founder and executive director of Power The Future, a national nonprofit organization that advocates for American energy jobs. body:

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it's Gina.
**The future of public education for _5.5 million Texas children_ is on the ballot this November.**
For over a decade, Greg Abbott and his appointed Texas Education Agency Commissioner, Mike Morath, have starved our public schools, pushed standardized testing, and funneled taxpayer dollars into private school vouchers.
**Right now, 70% of voucher funds are going to families already in private school or homeschooling.**
As a former school board president and public school mom, I will fire Mike Morath on Day 1 and replace him with a career classroom teacher.
I will end private school vouchers, eliminate high-stakes STAAR testing, stop state takeovers of local school boards, and redirect wasteful vendor spending straight into teacher paychecks.
Public education is the foundation of Texas's future, and we can’t let Greg Abbott continue to dismantle it.

name: Paige for Congress
subject: ✊🏻 Disruptive Compassion Lives On
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Paige Beauchemin for Congress
body:
| |
---
Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Friends, It has been a tremendous honor to run for Congress with you. When we launched this campaign last October, this team was filled with hope and excitement. We knew we were starting a movement for everyday people. Over the past eleven months, with your help, we accomplished so much. We held multiple mutual aid drives to support New Hampshire communities. We organized to prevent an ICE detention center from coming to our state. We made thousands of connections through thousands of conversations. We amplified important messages and pushed the NH politics left.

None of that would have been possible without each and every one of you. Thank you to every single donor, large and small, who supported the campaign financially. Thank you to the core team who managed the strategic operations, on a completely volunteer basis. Thank you to the volunteers who made buttons, folded zines, coordinated events, delivered signs, made T-shirts, and more.

We felt the support from afar as well: reading our emails, following and liking us on social media, and talking to people in your life about the movement.

Though we didn't get one of the outcomes we worked so hard for, what we built together does not end here. The support you put behind me, a working person, sent a clear message: People want something different. People want representation that answers to them, not the wealthy few. We challenged the status quo. Our calls for change were heard, and they will continue. I'm a fighter, and I will keep raising my voice, even if it's not from D.C. There is so much ahead, and I will continue to send you periodic updates. Stay tuned. Raise your voice too. Carry a love that fights and disruptive compassion into everything you do. The fight for our **power, prosperity, and peace** doesn't end with this campaign. In many ways, we've only just begun, even if our work looks a little different going forward. In Solidarity, ~ Paige
---
|
---

Friend, Labor Day didn't start as a three-day weekend. It started because workers organized for dignity, fair pay, and a voice on the job. My Dad was a union leader. He spent three decades at the U.S. Post Office. I owe my activist streak to him. He's the reason I speak up for others and fight for what's right. That's what led me to become a union leader myself during my time at the U.S. Government Accountability Office, where I helped raise wages and secure better benefits and working conditions for thousands of federal workers. In Congress, I'll keep fighting for that same dignity and fair pay for every worker, including the right to organize, because that fight is exactly what built the holiday we just celebrated. I recently traveled to Presidio and Terlingua, Texas to meet with the communities that will be directly impacted by the federal government's plans to build a border wall in the Big Bend region. In case you missed it, the federal government awarded $1.7 billion in Department of Homeland Security contracts to build six-foot and thirty-foot steel bollard walls, vehicle barriers, and patrol roads around Big Bend National Park, Big Bend Ranch State Park, and its surrounding areas. This poses an environmental and economic threat not to just the national parks that we know and love but to the actual people who make a living and rely on cross-border relationships to thrive.
Big Bend holds enormous cultural, archaeological, and environmental significance for Texans. Border wall construction along the Rio Grande threatens more than the landscape -- it could disrupt river tourism, ranching and agriculture, and the communities whose livelihoods depend on the land and water.
**I am so proud that the people of the Big Bend region have been fighting to protect what is sacred land, and as governor, I will fight to protect our sovereignty and the inheritance of the Big Bend so that our children and grandchildren can experience what we have here.**
The beauty of Big Bend is such a gift that we have in Texas, and we have to fight for it and preserve it. Big Bend's remote, rugged landscape -- marked by mountains, desert, steep canyons, and rough terrain -- already creates significant natural barriers to movement across the region. Which begs the question: _Why are there plans to carve out a physical barrier to this natural landscape in the first place?_
There has been very little transparency about how the federal government decided on what it plans to build, how many people will be displaced by this project, and the environmental consequences of construction. In fact, the Department of Homeland Security waived numerous environmental laws -- including the Endangered Species Act -- to fast track this project.
Plans have shifted repeatedly, even as billions of dollars in contracts have already been awarded and construction activity has moved forward. Texans deserve clear answers about what is being built in our backyard and what we stand to lose. Anyone who has experienced the beauty of Big Bend, understands that what is happening now is just a travesty.
Instead of actually fighting to protect Texans and our land, Greg Abbott has taken credit for the months-long campaign led by local grassroots activists to pause construction within the area -- a pause that came after land owners had to file a federal lawsuit. If we had a governor who cared to defend our sovereignty and our land, everyday Texans would not have to be carrying that burden. Abbot should have sued the federal government to stop what is happening in Big Bend. **His lack of leadership on this issue is shameful. Texans should not have to wait until bulldozers arrive for their governor to defend our land.**
A temporary pause won't change what has already been bulldozed -- this landscape has been permanently altered, we cannot simply put it back the way it was. And there's no telling what will happen when the construction pause ends at the end of this month. That is why this fight is urgent and requires all of us to keep speaking out in defense of Big Bend.
As governor, I will fight to protect Big Bend and the Texans who call this region home. I will demand transparency from the federal government, stand with communities challenging destructive projects, and use every legal tool available to defend Texas land and our sovereignty.
Big Bend belongs to all of us -- and we owe it to the generations that come after us to fight for it now.
I am so grateful to have met with the local business owners, preservationists, and community members within the region who help keep Big Bend the special place that it is. Please, take a look at the gallery below to see some of the people and places that made my visit so meaningful:
Credit: Photography by Hannah Gentiles
Thank you for fighting back,
Gina

clean_body: Greg Abbott's refusal to protect the Big Bend region is yet another example of his failed leadership | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Greg Abbott's refusal to protect the Big Bend region is yet another example of his failed leadership | | | Sep 12 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- I recently traveled to Presidio and Terlingua, Texas to meet with the communities that will be directly impacted by the federal government's plans to build a border wall in the Big Bend region. In case you missed it, the federal government awarded $1.7 billion in Department of Homeland Security contracts to build six-foot and thirty-foot steel bollard walls, vehicle barriers, and patrol roads around Big Bend National Park, Big Bend Ranch State Park, and its surrounding areas. This poses an environmental and economic threat not to just the national parks that we know and love but to the actual people who make a living and rely on cross-border relationships to thrive. Big Bend holds enormous cultural, archaeological, and environmental significance for Texans. Border wall construction along the Rio Grande threatens more than the landscape -- it could disrupt river tourism, ranching and agriculture, and the communities whose livelihoods depend on the land and water. I am so proud that the people of the Big Bend region have been fighting to protect what is sacred land, and as governor, I will fight to protect our sovereignty and the inheritance of the Big Bend so that our children and grandchildren can experience what we have here. The beauty of Big Bend is such a gift that we have in Texas, and we have to fight for it and preserve it. Big Bend's remote, rugged landscape -- marked by mountains, desert, steep canyons, and rough terrain -- already creates significant natural barriers to movement across the region. Which begs the question: Why are there plans to carve out a physical barrier to this natural landscape in the first place? There has been very little transparency about how the federal government decided on what it plans to build, how many people will be displaced by this project, and the environmental consequences of construction. In fact, the Department of Homeland Security waived numerous environmental laws -- including the Endangered Species Act -- to fast track this project. Plans have shifted repeatedly, even as billions of dollars in contracts have already been awarded and construction activity has moved forward. Texans deserve clear answers about what is being built in our backyard and what we stand to lose. Anyone who has experienced the beauty of Big Bend, understands that what is happening now is just a travesty. Instead of actually fighting to protect Texans and our land, Greg Abbott has taken credit for the months-long campaign led by local grassroots activists to pause construction within the area -- a pause that came after land owners had to file a federal lawsuit. If we had a governor who cared to defend our sovereignty and our land, everyday Texans would not have to be carrying that burden. Abbot should have sued the federal government to stop what is happening in Big Bend. His lack of leadership on this issue is shameful. Texans should not have to wait until bulldozers arrive for their governor to defend our land. A temporary pause won't change what has already been bulldozed -- this landscape has been permanently altered, we cannot simply put it back the way it was. And there's no telling what will happen when the construction pause ends at the end of this month. That is why this fight is urgent and requires all of us to keep speaking out in defense of Big Bend. As governor, I will fight to protect Big Bend and the Texans who call this region home. I will demand transparency from the federal government, stand with communities challenging destructive projects, and use every legal tool available to defend Texas land and our sovereignty. Big Bend belongs to all of us -- and we owe it to the generations that come after us to fight for it now. I am so grateful to have met with the local business owners, preservationists, and community members within the region who help keep Big Bend the special place that it is. Please, take a look at the gallery below to see some of the people and places that made my visit so meaningful: Credit: Photography by Hannah Gentiles Thank you for fighting back, Gina * | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Gina Hinojosa PO Box 300095, Austin, TX 78703 ? ?
